modules.title: USE and RED: Two Lenses on One System
modules.purpose: Choose the right signal set for a resource problem or a service problem
modules.productionQuestion: Is this a resource problem or a request-path problem, and which signal set tells you first?
modules.learningDelta: USE finds saturated resources; RED finds sick request paths; using one where the other belongs hides the cause

modules.title: Little's Law: Concurrency, Latency, Throughput
modules.purpose: Size concurrency and queues from two numbers instead of guessing
modules.productionQuestion: Throughput is flat and latency is rising: how much concurrency is actually in the system?
modules.learningDelta: L = λW ties concurrency, arrival rate, and time in system; rising latency at fixed throughput means work is piling up

modules.title: The Queueing Knee: Why 70% Is the New 100%
modules.purpose: Predict the latency cliff before utilization reaches saturation
modules.productionQuestion: CPU is at 75% and p99 doubled; is the system healthy?
modules.learningDelta: Queueing latency is nonlinear; near saturation, small load increases create large latency increases

modules.title: Percentiles: What the Average Hides
modules.purpose: Read tail latency without being fooled by averages
modules.productionQuestion: Mean latency is 80ms and p99 is 1.9s; which number describes the user experience?
modules.learningDelta: Averages hide tail pain; p99 and p999 describe the slow requests that drive timeouts and retries

modules.title: Coordinated Omission: The Metric That Lies
modules.purpose: Detect a load generator or metric pipeline that hides stalls
modules.productionQuestion: Your load test reports p99 120ms but users report 4s stalls. What is wrong with the measurement?
modules.learningDelta: Closed-loop generators stop issuing requests during a stall, so slow samples are omitted; latency must be measured against intended arrival time

modules.title: SLI, SLO, SLA, and the Error Budget
modules.purpose: Turn reliability into a measurable budget instead of a feeling
modules.productionQuestion: Your SLO is 99.9% and the month is half over; how much failure can you still spend?
modules.learningDelta: An error budget converts an SLO into an allowed failure quantity; burn rate tells you when to stop shipping

modules.title: Capacity Headroom and N+1
modules.purpose: Survive one failure domain without breaching SLO
modules.productionQuestion: You are at 60% peak utilization with three AZs; what happens when one AZ is lost?
modules.learningDelta: N+1 headroom must cover the loss of the largest failure domain at peak, not at average

modules.title: Idempotency: Retries Without Duplicate Side Effects
modules.purpose: Make retried writes safe under timeouts and ambiguous failures
modules.productionQuestion: The payment timed out; did it charge the customer, and is it safe to retry?
modules.learningDelta: An idempotency key makes a retried write return the original result instead of creating a second effect

modules.title: Timeouts: Budgets That Travel With the Request
modules.purpose: Prevent one slow dependency from consuming the whole request budget
modules.productionQuestion: A request has 800ms total and three calls; which timeout do you set?
modules.learningDelta: Timeouts must be smaller than the caller's remaining budget and must propagate a deadline, not restart it

modules.title: Retries, Backoff, and Jitter
modules.purpose: Stop a retry policy from becoming a self-inflicted DDoS
modules.productionQuestion: A dependency returns 503 for two seconds; why did traffic triple?
modules.learningDelta: Synchronized retries amplify failure; exponential backoff with jitter spreads retries and caps amplification

modules.title: Circuit Breaking: Fail Fast, Recover Slowly
modules.purpose: Stop sending traffic to a dependency that is already failing
modules.productionQuestion: The dependency is timing out; how do you stop making it worse without manual intervention?
modules.learningDelta: A breaker converts repeated failures into fast local failures and probes recovery with limited traffic

modules.title: Bulkheads: Isolate the Blast Radius
modules.purpose: Keep one tenant or workload from consuming a shared pool
modules.productionQuestion: One tenant's batch job is starving interactive traffic; how do you isolate it?
modules.learningDelta: Pools, queues, and concurrency limits per workload contain saturation to one bulkhead

modules.title: Load Shedding: Protect Goodput
modules.purpose: Choose which requests to reject when demand exceeds capacity
modules.productionQuestion: The system can serve 10k RPS and receives 30k; what should it do?
modules.learningDelta: Beyond capacity, serving everything degrades goodput; shedding low-value work early preserves useful throughput

modules.title: Graceful Degradation: Cut Features, Keep Promises
modules.purpose: Keep the critical path up when a non-critical dependency fails
modules.productionQuestion: Recommendations are down and the product is timing out; what do you disable first?
modules.learningDelta: Degradation is a designed dependency hierarchy; non-critical work must fail without taking the core path

modules.title: CAP and PACELC: The Trade You Cannot Avoid
modules.purpose: Explain consistency and availability choices without slogans
modules.productionQuestion: The network partition is real; which writes do you accept and which do you refuse?
modules.learningDelta: CAP applies only during partitions; PACELC extends the tradeoff to latency versus consistency in normal operation

modules.title: Consistency Models: What a Read Can Promise
modules.purpose: Choose the weakest model that satisfies the product
modules.productionQuestion: A user updates a profile and immediately sees the old value; which consistency guarantee is missing?
modules.learningDelta: Strong, read-your-writes, monotonic, and eventual consistency are different promises with different costs

modules.title: Linux CPU Saturation: Run Queue and Steal
modules.purpose: Tell real CPU pressure from a busy-looking graph
modules.productionQuestion: CPU is at 60% but latency is high; is the host actually saturated?
modules.learningDelta: Run-queue length, steal time, and per-core saturation reveal CPU pressure that a smoothed utilization average hides

modules.title: Linux Memory: Page Cache, RSS, and OOM
modules.purpose: Find the real memory consumer before the kernel kills a process
modules.productionQuestion: The host reports 90% memory used but nothing is swapping; is it about to OOM?
modules.learningDelta: Page cache is reclaimable; anonymous memory, kernel memory, and cgroup limits decide OOM behavior

modules.title: Disk I/O: IOPS, Queue Depth, and fsync
modules.purpose: Diagnose storage latency under write pressure
modules.productionQuestion: Disk utilization is 100% and writes take 300ms; is the device slow or overloaded?
modules.learningDelta: IOPS, throughput, and queue depth are different limits; fsync latency exposes durability cost

modules.title: Network Saturation: Bandwidth, Retransmits, and Drops
modules.purpose: Distinguish a full pipe from a lossy path
modules.productionQuestion: Throughput is below the link rate and latency climbs; what network signal do you check first?
modules.learningDelta: Bandwidth, packet loss, retransmits, and NIC queue drops are different failure modes with different fixes

modules.title: File Descriptors: The Invisible Capacity Limit
modules.purpose: Find an fd leak before it becomes a full outage
modules.productionQuestion: The service is healthy but new connections fail with “too many open files”; where do you look?
modules.learningDelta: Every socket and file consumes an fd; per-process and system limits turn leaks into hard failures

modules.title: Conntrack Exhaustion: When NAT Forgets
modules.purpose: Diagnose connection drops caused by the NAT table
modules.productionQuestion: New connections fail intermittently while established traffic is fine; what table is full?
modules.learningDelta: Conntrack entries track NAT flows; exhaustion and short timeouts drop new connections even when bandwidth is free

modules.title: TLS Handshakes: Latency Before the Request
modules.purpose: Separate handshake cost from request cost
modules.productionQuestion: p99 rose after a DNS change; is TLS or the application slow?
modules.learningDelta: Full handshakes add round trips and CPU; resumption and keep-alive remove them from the steady state

modules.title: HTTP/2 and Keep-Alive: Reuse With Rules
modules.purpose: Diagnose connection churn caused by mismatched idle timeouts
modules.productionQuestion: The load balancer is healthy but backends see a new connection per request; why?
modules.learningDelta: Connection reuse depends on both peers agreeing on idle timeouts, max requests, and protocol; mismatches cause churn

modules.title: Connection Pools: Queue Before the Database
modules.purpose: Size a pool from capacity, not from hope
modules.productionQuestion: The database allows 500 connections and the service has 40 tasks; what pool size?
modules.learningDelta: Pool size is a queueing decision; too small waits, too large multiplies database sessions and contention

modules.title: Password Hashing: Cost, Salt, and Timing
modules.purpose: Store passwords without creating a fast offline target
modules.productionQuestion: A leaked database contains unsalted SHA-256 hashes; what did the team get wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Password hashing uses a unique salt and a tunable work factor (bcrypt/Argon2); fast general-purpose hashes are the wrong tool

modules.title: Rate Limiting: Token Bucket vs Fixed Window
modules.purpose: Enforce a rate without allowing boundary bursts
modules.productionQuestion: A fixed-window limiter allows 2× the intended rate at the window boundary; how do you fix it?
modules.learningDelta: Token bucket smooths average rate while allowing a bounded burst; fixed windows permit boundary spikes

modules.title: Caching Strategies: Where the Write Goes
modules.purpose: Choose cache-aside, write-through, or write-behind for a workload
modules.productionQuestion: The product needs fast reads and durable writes; which cache strategy fits?
modules.learningDelta: Cache-aside keeps the cache optional, write-through keeps it fresh at write cost, write-behind risks data loss

modules.title: Cache Invalidation: Coherence Without Guessing
modules.purpose: Keep cached reads fresh across many app instances
modules.productionQuestion: An update lands on one instance and other instances serve stale data for minutes; how do you invalidate?
modules.learningDelta: Invalidation is a distributed coherence problem; pub/sub, versioned keys, and short TTLs trade freshness for complexity

modules.title: Admission Control: Bounded Queues and Priorities
modules.purpose: Reject work early instead of timing out late
modules.productionQuestion: The queue is 30 seconds deep and clients time out before service; what should the server do?
modules.learningDelta: Admission control keeps queues bounded and rejects or prioritizes work before latency becomes useless

modules.title: Backpressure: Make the Producer Slow Down
modules.purpose: Stop a fast producer from turning a queue into a memory bomb
modules.productionQuestion: The consumer is slower than the producer and the queue is growing; where does backpressure belong?
modules.learningDelta: Backpressure propagates capacity signals upstream; bounded queues and producer throttling prevent unbounded memory and latency

modules.title: Failure Domains: Blast Radius by Design
modules.purpose: Bound the impact of the next failure
modules.productionQuestion: A single rack failure took down the service despite three AZs; what was correlated?
modules.learningDelta: Independent failure domains require independent power, network, deployment, and dependency paths, not just AZ labels

modules.title: Golden Signals: Latency, Traffic, Errors, Saturation
modules.purpose: Build a first-response dashboard that exposes the request-path health
modules.productionQuestion: CPU is normal, the dashboard is green, and users are complaining. Which signal did you not graph?
modules.learningDelta: The four golden signals answer different questions; saturation can hide while latency, errors, or traffic already show the incident

modules.title: Counters, Gauges, and Histograms
modules.purpose: Use the right metric type so the query means what you think
modules.productionQuestion: A counter is reset by a deploy and the error graph goes negative. What type or query is wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Counters need rate(), gauges are point-in-time, histograms support quantiles; mixing them produces nonsense

modules.title: PromQL Rate: Windows, Resets, and Aliasing
modules.purpose: Read rate() correctly across scrape intervals and counter resets
modules.productionQuestion: Your rate query shows spikes every minute that do not match user impact. Why?
modules.learningDelta: rate() extrapolates over a window; the window must cover several scrapes and align with the counter's reset behavior

modules.title: Histogram Quantiles: Buckets Decide the Tail
modules.purpose: Avoid confident p99 answers from bad bucket boundaries
modules.productionQuestion: The p99 panel says 200ms but traces show 2s requests. Which is wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Histogram quantiles are interpolated within buckets; poor bucket layout hides the tail and cannot exceed the largest bucket

modules.title: Dashboards That Answer One Question
modules.purpose: Design a dashboard around a decision, not a data dump
modules.productionQuestion: An on-call engineer opens the dashboard and cannot decide whether to roll back. What is missing?
modules.learningDelta: A dashboard is a decision aid: one question, ordered signals, thresholds, and links to the next check

modules.title: Datadog Tags and Cardinality
modules.purpose: Control tag cardinality before it changes cost and query behavior
modules.productionQuestion: A new tag contains user IDs and the metric bill tripled. What happened?
modules.learningDelta: Each unique tag combination creates a time series; high-cardinality tags multiply storage, query cost, and billing

modules.title: Custom Metric Cost: The Multiplier Stack
modules.purpose: Estimate observability cost before adding a metric
modules.productionQuestion: One custom metric across hosts and tags looks cheap in the UI; what does it cost at scale?
modules.learningDelta: Custom metric cost multiplies metric name, hosts, and tag combinations; a small tag change can dominate the bill

modules.title: APM Sampling: See the Errors That Matter
modules.purpose: Configure APM sampling without losing rare failures
modules.productionQuestion: Trace sampling is 1% and a 0.2% error class is invisible. How do you sample?
modules.learningDelta: Uniform head sampling is cheap but blind to rare errors; retention and error-biased sampling preserve the traces you need

modules.title: VictoriaMetrics Architecture: Ingest, Store, Query
modules.purpose: Explain where a VictoriaMetrics deployment loses telemetry
modules.productionQuestion: Metrics arrive late and queries time out during a rollout. Which VictoriaMetrics component is the bottleneck?
modules.learningDelta: vminsert, vmstorage, and vmselect have separate scaling limits; ingestion, storage, and query pressure must be diagnosed separately

modules.title: VictoriaMetrics and High Cardinality
modules.purpose: Keep high-cardinality metrics queryable without exhausting storage
modules.productionQuestion: A label with request IDs makes the series count explode. What happens to memory and query time?
modules.learningDelta: Series cardinality drives index and memory cost; high-cardinality labels belong in logs or traces, not metric labels

modules.title: Retention and Downsampling Tradeoffs
modules.purpose: Match retention to audits, incidents, and cost
modules.productionQuestion: Compliance needs one year, dashboards need 30 days, and disk is full. What do you keep?
modules.learningDelta: Retention tiers and downsampling preserve long-range trends while reducing resolution and cost

modules.title: OpenTelemetry Context Propagation
modules.purpose: Keep one trace across services and async boundaries
modules.productionQuestion: The trace stops at the queue consumer and shows two unrelated traces. What broke?
modules.learningDelta: Trace context must be injected and extracted across every hop, including queues and background jobs

modules.title: Head Sampling: Cheap and Blind
modules.purpose: Set a head sampling rate with known blind spots
modules.productionQuestion: A 5% head sample makes a rare error class invisible. What is the tradeoff?
modules.learningDelta: Head sampling decides before the request outcome is known; it is cheap and unbiased for volume but unreliable for rare outcomes

modules.title: Tail Sampling: Keep the Interesting Traces
modules.purpose: Retain errors and slow traces without storing everything
modules.productionQuestion: Storage budget allows 2% of traces, but you need every timeout. How do you sample?
modules.learningDelta: Tail sampling buffers completed traces and applies policies, preserving errors and latency outliers at bounded volume

modules.title: Structured Logging: Fields Over Sentences
modules.purpose: Make logs queryable at 3 a.m.
modules.productionQuestion: You need every log line for one request across 20 tasks. What must the log schema contain?
modules.learningDelta: Structured fields, request IDs, and stable event names make logs searchable; prose logs do not

modules.title: PII Redaction in Telemetry
modules.purpose: Keep personal data out of logs, traces, and metrics
modules.productionQuestion: A debug log contains an email and a token. What is your containment plan?
modules.learningDelta: Redaction must happen at emit time and be verified; logs and traces are copies of production data with different retention

modules.title: Distributed Tracing: Spans and Causality
modules.purpose: Read a trace as a critical path, not a pretty waterfall
modules.productionQuestion: A trace shows 12 spans and the slow one is not the service you expected. How do you read it?
modules.learningDelta: A trace is a causal tree; parent/child timing and span kind reveal where time is spent and where it is waited on

modules.title: Critical Path: Where the Time Actually Goes
modules.purpose: Avoid blaming the slowest service when it is waiting on another
modules.productionQuestion: Service B is slow and Service C is fast, yet C is on the critical path. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Span self-time and waiting time distinguish work from blocked time; the longest span is not always the cause

modules.title: SLO Burn Rate: Alert on Speed, Not Just State
modules.purpose: Page before the error budget is gone, not after
modules.productionQuestion: The 30-day SLO is still 99.9%, but the service has been failing for 40 minutes. Should you page?
modules.learningDelta: Multi-window burn-rate alerts catch fast burns early and slow burns reliably without paging on every blip

modules.title: Symptom-Based Alerting
modules.purpose: Alert on user pain, not on every possible cause
modules.productionQuestion: The CPU alert pages every night at 2 a.m. and users are fine. What should page instead?
modules.learningDelta: Symptom alerts track SLO impact; cause alerts support diagnosis but create noise and do not prove user impact

modules.title: Alert Fatigue: Measure Actionability
modules.purpose: Reduce paging load without losing real incidents
modules.productionQuestion: The team gets 60 pages a week and ignores half. Which alerts should exist?
modules.learningDelta: Alert quality is measured by actionable pages per incident; every noisy page trains responders to ignore the next one

modules.title: Anomaly Detection Pitfalls
modules.purpose: Use anomaly detection without paging on normal seasonality
modules.productionQuestion: The detector pages every Monday at 9 a.m. and no one is surprised. What is wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Statistical anomalies are not incidents; seasonality, trends, and missing data create false positives that need guardrails

modules.title: One Dashboard, One Decision
modules.purpose: Replace data-dump dashboards with decision paths
modules.productionQuestion: It is 3 a.m. and the dashboard has every metric but no next step. How do you redesign it?
modules.learningDelta: A useful dashboard orders signals by the decision they support and links the next check, not every available metric

modules.title: Synthetic Monitoring: Probe the Path
modules.purpose: Detect regional and edge failures before users report them
modules.productionQuestion: Users in one region cannot reach the app while your servers are healthy. What probes reveal it?
modules.learningDelta: Synthetic probes exercise the real path from multiple locations; interval and location coverage determine detection time

modules.title: RUM and Core Web Vitals
modules.purpose: See the browser experience your server metrics miss
modules.productionQuestion: Server p95 is 200ms but mobile users see a 4s LCP. Where do you look?
modules.learningDelta: RUM captures real device, network, and rendering performance; field percentiles differ from lab and server metrics

modules.title: Continuous Profiling: Find the Hot Function
modules.purpose: Locate CPU and allocation hotspots in production
modules.productionQuestion: Latency rose after a release and traces point to one service. Which function is burning CPU?
modules.learningDelta: Continuous profiles aggregate stack samples; flame graphs show self time and call paths that metrics and traces cannot

modules.title: Log Volume and Cost
modules.purpose: Keep debug logs without paying for all of them
modules.productionQuestion: A verbose release multiplies log volume and the ingestion budget is gone. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Log cost is volume × retention; level, sampling, and routing keep high-value logs while cutting noise

modules.title: Reconstructing the Incident Timeline
modules.purpose: Build a defensible timeline from telemetry and events
modules.productionQuestion: The postmortem says the rollback started at 14:20 but the graphs disagree. Which clock do you trust?
modules.learningDelta: Timelines require synchronized timestamps, deploy markers, and event sources; clock skew and missing annotations create false causality

modules.title: Scrape Interval and Resolution
modules.purpose: Match collection rate to the question being asked
modules.productionQuestion: A 15-second scrape cannot show a 5-second spike. What do you change, and what does it cost?
modules.learningDelta: Sampling resolution bounds what you can detect; shorter intervals improve detection but increase ingest and cost

modules.title: Exemplars: From Metric to Trace
modules.purpose: Jump from a slow histogram bucket to a real trace
modules.productionQuestion: p99 is high and you need one concrete slow request. How do you get from the graph to the trace?
modules.learningDelta: Exemplars attach trace IDs to metric samples, connecting aggregates to individual requests without storing every trace

modules.title: Log Pipeline Backpressure
modules.purpose: Prevent observability from failing during the incident
modules.productionQuestion: The log agent queue is full during a traffic spike and logs are dropped. How do you protect the pipeline?
modules.learningDelta: Agents need bounded buffers and prioritization; dropping debug logs is better than blocking application threads or losing errors

modules.title: Monitoring the Monitor
modules.purpose: Detect blind spots in the observability system itself
modules.productionQuestion: All dashboards are green and no metrics have arrived for 20 minutes. What now?
modules.learningDelta: Meta-monitoring checks scrape health, agent liveness, ingestion lag, and alert delivery; absence of data is itself an alert

modules.title: Error Tracking: Grouping and Fingerprints
modules.purpose: Keep distinct failures from collapsing into one issue
modules.productionQuestion: One error group has 40k events and three unrelated root causes. How do you split it?
modules.learningDelta: Error grouping uses fingerprints; stable, specific fingerprints preserve distinct causes without exploding issue count

modules.title: Telemetry Cost Governance
modules.purpose: Keep observability affordable as the system grows
modules.productionQuestion: Telemetry cost grows faster than traffic and no one owns it. What is the governance model?
modules.learningDelta: Cost governance uses budgets, cardinality limits, sampling, retention tiers, and ownership; observability is a product with a unit cost

modules.title: L4 vs L7: Choose the Right Load Balancer
modules.purpose: Place a transport or application load balancer for the traffic shape
modules.productionQuestion: You need static IPs and millions of connections, but also path routing. Which layer do you choose?
modules.learningDelta: L4 routes connections and cannot inspect paths; L7 routes requests and terminates protocols; the correct design often layers both

modules.title: ALB Target Groups: Registration and Health
modules.purpose: Get targets registered and healthy before tuning anything else
modules.productionQuestion: The ALB returns 503 while the tasks are running and healthy. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: An ALB only routes to healthy registered targets; health check path, port, and security groups decide registration

modules.title: Health Checks: Fast Detection vs Flapping
modules.purpose: Tune health checks without causing outages or false recovery
modules.productionQuestion: A single slow health check removed every task at once. What settings caused it?
modules.learningDelta: Interval, timeout, healthy/unhealthy thresholds, and grace period trade detection speed against false positives

modules.title: ALB Connection Limit Reached: Sharding to NLB
modules.purpose: Diagnose a per-ALB connection bottleneck and shard without breaking routing
modules.productionQuestion: Your ALB is healthy, targets are healthy, and you raised the capacity ceiling. New connections are still dropped at peak. What now?
modules.learningDelta: ALB scale limits are per load balancer and per node; at scale you shard across ALBs behind an NLB, not just raise a single ceiling

modules.title: ALB LCU: Capacity and Cost Together
modules.purpose: Predict when ALB cost and capacity become the constraint
modules.productionQuestion: The bill doubled after a traffic change and the ALB is near its LCU limit. Which dimension moved?
modules.learningDelta: LCU bills the highest of new connections, active connections, processed bytes, and rule evaluations; the same traffic can be limited by different dimensions

modules.title: NLB in Front of ALB: What It Buys and Costs
modules.purpose: Layer an NLB for static IPs and scale without losing path routing
modules.productionQuestion: You need static IPs and ALB path routing at very high connection counts. How do you combine them?
modules.learningDelta: An NLB can front ALBs with static IPs and high connection capacity, adding a hop and changing source-IP and TLS behavior

modules.title: Sharding ALBs by Tenant or Hostname
modules.purpose: Spread connections across ALBs without breaking sessions
modules.productionQuestion: One tenant's traffic saturates its ALB while other ALBs are idle. How do you shard?
modules.learningDelta: Sharding by hostname, path, or tenant reduces per-ALB connection pressure but requires routing consistency and per-shard observability

modules.title: Cross-Zone Load Balancing
modules.purpose: Balance across zones without paying hidden latency or transfer costs
modules.productionQuestion: Two AZs have healthy targets, but one AZ gets most traffic. What setting explains it?
modules.learningDelta: Cross-zone balancing distributes across healthy targets in all zones; disabling it isolates zones but can strand capacity

modules.title: Zonal Isolation: Survive an AZ Loss
modules.purpose: Keep serving when one availability zone fails
modules.productionQuestion: One AZ is impaired and the service degrades more than expected. What shared dependency crossed zones?
modules.learningDelta: Zonal isolation requires independent targets, load balancer nodes, NAT, and dependencies per zone

modules.title: Sticky Sessions: Affinity and Its Cost
modules.purpose: Keep sessions working without creating hot targets
modules.productionQuestion: A session-heavy app loses carts when targets scale in. What is the tradeoff of stickiness?
modules.learningDelta: Sticky sessions preserve affinity but reduce load balance, complicate draining, and can concentrate load on a few targets

modules.title: Connection Draining and Deregistration Delay
modules.purpose: Remove targets without cutting active requests
modules.productionQuestion: A rolling deploy causes 502s even though the new tasks are healthy. What setting do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Deregistration delay lets in-flight requests finish before a target is removed; too short cuts requests, too long slows deploys

modules.title: DNS TTL and Failover
modules.purpose: Understand how slow DNS makes failover slow
modules.productionQuestion: You changed the DNS record but clients still hit the failed region after 10 minutes. Why?
modules.learningDelta: DNS failover is bounded by TTL and resolver caching; applications and JVMs may cache longer than the record TTL

modules.title: Route 53 Health Checks
modules.purpose: Detect endpoint failure from the edge
modules.productionQuestion: Route 53 still sends traffic to a dead region. What does its health check actually observe?
modules.learningDelta: Route 53 health checks probe endpoints from multiple locations and can be calculated or CloudWatch-backed; thresholds determine failover speed

modules.title: Route 53 Routing Policies
modules.purpose: Choose failover, weighted, latency, or geolocation deliberately
modules.productionQuestion: You need gradual regional migration with fast rollback. Which routing policy fits?
modules.learningDelta: Weighted routing shifts traffic gradually; failover is binary; latency optimizes user location; geolocation enforces locality

modules.title: Anycast: Same IP, Many Places
modules.purpose: Explain global entry without a single global box
modules.productionQuestion: Users worldwide hit one IP but land in different regions. How does that work, and what breaks?
modules.learningDelta: Anycast advertises the same prefix from many sites; BGP chooses a path, so routing changes can shift traffic and create asymmetric failures

modules.title: CDN Cache Keys: Hit Rate by Design
modules.purpose: Raise cache hit rate without serving the wrong content
modules.productionQuestion: CDN hit rate is 30% and origin is overloaded. What belongs in the cache key?
modules.learningDelta: Cache key selection decides reuse; including irrelevant headers fragments the cache, omitting vary-worthy inputs serves wrong content

modules.title: CDN TTL and Purge
modules.purpose: Balance freshness, hit rate, and origin load
modules.productionQuestion: A deploy needs new assets immediately but long TTLs keep old ones cached. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: TTL trades freshness for hit rate; purge is fast but operationally risky and may not reach every edge immediately

modules.title: Origin Shield and Request Collapsing
modules.purpose: Protect the origin from a cache miss storm
modules.productionQuestion: A popular object expires and every edge requests it from the origin. How do you collapse the misses?
modules.learningDelta: Origin shield centralizes misses and request collapsing turns concurrent misses into one origin fetch

modules.title: WAF and Edge Rate Limits
modules.purpose: Block abusive traffic without blocking customers
modules.productionQuestion: A credential-stuffing wave is exhausting the login service. Where do you enforce limits?
modules.learningDelta: Edge WAF rules and rate limits stop abuse before compute, but thresholds and match conditions decide false positives

modules.title: DDoS and Shield: Absorb and Scrub
modules.purpose: Keep a volumetric attack from reaching the origin
modules.productionQuestion: Inbound traffic jumps 40× and the load balancer is dropping connections. What absorbs it?
modules.learningDelta: DDoS protection combines edge capacity, anycast scrubbing, and rate controls; origin capacity is not the defense

modules.title: HTTP/3 and QUIC
modules.purpose: Choose a transport for lossy mobile networks
modules.productionQuestion: Mobile users on lossy networks see slow loads over TCP. Would QUIC help, and what breaks?
modules.learningDelta: QUIC runs over UDP with independent streams and faster handshakes; loss affects streams differently but UDP may be blocked

modules.title: TLS Termination: Where Keys Live
modules.purpose: Terminate TLS at the right layer
modules.productionQuestion: You need end-to-end encryption but the ALB must route by path. Where do you terminate?
modules.learningDelta: TLS can terminate at edge, load balancer, or service; each choice changes certificate scope, inspection, and latency

modules.title: Keep-Alive and Idle Timeout Mismatch
modules.purpose: Stop connection churn between LB and targets
modules.productionQuestion: The ALB opens a new backend connection for almost every request. Which timeout is misaligned?
modules.learningDelta: Keep-alive must outlive the load balancer's idle timeout; if the backend closes first, requests race and connections churn

modules.title: Edge Rate Limiting: Protect the Origin
modules.purpose: Choose edge limits that preserve fairness
modules.productionQuestion: One API key sends 80% of requests and the origin is saturated. Where do you limit?
modules.learningDelta: Per-key, per-IP, and global limits solve different abuse; edge limits must account for NAT and shared clients

modules.title: Global Accelerator: Anycast for Your ALBs
modules.purpose: Reduce global latency and failover time without DNS TTL
modules.productionQuestion: Users on another continent see 300ms extra and DNS failover is too slow. What does Global Accelerator change?
modules.learningDelta: Global Accelerator uses anycast IPs and AWS backbone to reach regional endpoints; it removes DNS TTL from the failover path

modules.title: Debugging 502 Bad Gateway
modules.purpose: Distinguish a target failure from an edge failure
modules.productionQuestion: Users get 502s and the targets say they are healthy. Where do you look first?
modules.learningDelta: A 502 means the load balancer could not get a valid response from the target; health, protocol, keepalive, and connection reset are the suspects

modules.title: Debugging 503 Service Unavailable
modules.purpose: Tell capacity exhaustion from no registered targets
modules.productionQuestion: The ALB returns 503 but CPU is 40%. What are the possible causes?
modules.learningDelta: A 503 can be ELB-generated when no target is registered, or target-generated when a concurrency or pool limit rejects work; CPU alone does not explain it

modules.title: Debugging 504 Gateway Timeout
modules.purpose: Find which timeout actually fired
modules.productionQuestion: A request returns 504 after 60 seconds; the service logs show 2 seconds of work. Which timeout expired?
modules.learningDelta: A 504 means a timeout expired; it can be generated by the ALB or the target, and the upstream may still be working; align LB, service, and dependency budgets

modules.title: ALB Rule Priority and Order
modules.purpose: Prevent a broad rule from shadowing a specific one
modules.productionQuestion: A new host rule works in staging but not production. What wins?
modules.learningDelta: ALB listener rules evaluate in priority order; the first match wins, so broad rules can shadow specific ones

modules.title: Host and Path Routing
modules.purpose: Route tenants without breaking TLS or sessions
modules.productionQuestion: You need to route api.meridian.internal and app.meridian.internal to different services. Where does routing belong?
modules.learningDelta: Host/path routing at the ALB is cheap and centralized; it must account for certificates, wildcard scope, and rule limits

modules.title: WebSockets Through a Load Balancer
modules.purpose: Keep long-lived connections alive and balanced
modules.productionQuestion: WebSocket clients disconnect every 60 seconds behind the ALB. What setting is involved?
modules.learningDelta: WebSockets reuse a long-lived TCP connection; idle timeouts, draining, and connection limits behave differently from short HTTP requests

modules.title: gRPC Load Balancing
modules.purpose: Balance long-lived HTTP/2 streams per request
modules.productionQuestion: gRPC clients pin to one backend despite many replicas. Why?
modules.learningDelta: gRPC uses long-lived HTTP/2 connections; connection-level balancing pins streams, so request-level or proxy balancing is required

modules.title: Cloudflare and Akamai Behavior
modules.purpose: Compare edge cache, purge, and rule behavior across providers
modules.productionQuestion: The same cache rule behaves differently on two CDNs. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Edge providers implement cache keys, purge, and rule evaluation differently; portability requires testing the behavior you depend on

modules.title: Upstream Connection Reuse
modules.purpose: Stop connection storms after a deploy
modules.productionQuestion: Backends see a connection storm after every deploy even though traffic is flat. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Connection pools and keep-alive must be warmed and drained alongside targets; new targets without reuse multiply handshakes

modules.title: Redis Data Types and Their Cost
modules.purpose: Choose a data structure that fits access and memory
modules.productionQuestion: A leaderboard rewrite lowers latency but memory triples. Which data type caused it?
modules.learningDelta: Data type choice sets memory overhead, operation complexity, and atomicity; the wrong type makes a fast operation expensive at scale

modules.title: Redis Persistence: RDB, AOF, and Loss Windows
modules.purpose: Choose durability that matches the data, not the default
modules.productionQuestion: Redis restarts and 40 seconds of writes are gone. Which persistence setting was used?
modules.learningDelta: RDB snapshots lose writes between snapshots; AOF reduces the loss window at fsync cost; caching may not need either

modules.title: Eviction Policies: Protect the Working Set
modules.purpose: Keep the right keys when memory is full
modules.productionQuestion: Redis is at maxmemory and hit rate collapses. Which keys are being evicted?
modules.learningDelta: allkeys policies may evict hot data; volatile policies only evict keys with TTL; policy must match the cache's purpose

modules.title: Detecting a Hot Key
modules.purpose: Find the key causing uneven shard load
modules.productionQuestion: Shard CPU is uneven but no dashboard shows a hot key. How do you find it?
modules.learningDelta: Hot keys are visible in per-key command counts, latency, and shard imbalance; aggregate hit rate hides them

modules.title: Hot Key Sharding: One Key, One Saturated Shard
modules.purpose: Diagnose a hot key as a partitioning problem and compare fixes
modules.productionQuestion: One Redis key is getting 40% of traffic. Seven shards are idle and one is on fire. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: A hot key is a partitioning problem; salting, local caching, and read replicas solve different parts of it, and resizing the cache does not

modules.title: Hot Shard in Redis Cluster
modules.purpose: Separate a hot key from a hot hash slot
modules.productionQuestion: One hash slot is saturated while the cluster has free capacity. Can you move the slot?
modules.learningDelta: Redis Cluster distributes keys by hash slot; a hot key and its co-located keys share a shard, and resharding cannot split one key

modules.title: Key Salting: Spread One Key Across Shards
modules.purpose: Reduce hot-key concentration without breaking reads
modules.productionQuestion: Salting a key spreads load but changes every reader. How do you migrate safely?
modules.learningDelta: Salting adds a deterministic suffix to fan a hot key across shards; it requires reading all salted variants and a migration plan

modules.title: Read Replicas: Offload Without Staleness Surprises
modules.purpose: Add read capacity without breaking freshness
modules.productionQuestion: Read replicas cut Redis CPU but users see stale data. What is the tradeoff?
modules.learningDelta: Replicas offload reads but replicate asynchronously; lag creates staleness, and hot-key reads can saturate a replica instead

modules.title: Cache Stampede: When TTL Expires at the Wrong Time
modules.purpose: Prevent an expired key from sending a wave to the database
modules.productionQuestion: A popular key expires and the database CPU goes to 100%. How do you stop the herd?
modules.learningDelta: A stampede occurs when many concurrent misses recompute one value; single-flight, jitter, and early refresh collapse the work

modules.title: Request Coalescing: One Miss, One Fetch
modules.purpose: Turn concurrent misses into one backend call
modules.productionQuestion: Fifty requests miss the same key at once. How many database queries should run?
modules.learningDelta: Single-flight coalescing lets one request compute while others wait or receive stale data; it trades latency for backend protection

modules.title: Probabilistic Early Expiration
modules.purpose: Refresh hot values before they expire
modules.productionQuestion: A hot key expires in sync across all app instances. How do you refresh early?
modules.learningDelta: Probabilistic early expiration spreads refreshes before TTL expiry, reducing synchronized misses at the cost of extra recomputation

modules.title: TTL Jitter and Smearing
modules.purpose: Break synchronized expiry across a fleet
modules.productionQuestion: A batch warmup gives every key the same TTL and the cache expires in waves. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: TTL jitter spreads expiration, smoothing backend load and reducing synchronized refreshes

modules.title: Local Cache + Redis
modules.purpose: Absorb hot reads before they reach the network
modules.productionQuestion: Redis p99 is fine but one hot key consumes most of its capacity. Is a local cache safe?
modules.learningDelta: An in-process cache removes network hops for hot reads but introduces per-instance staleness and memory cost

modules.title: Cache Coherence Across Instances
modules.purpose: Invalidate local and remote caches reliably
modules.productionQuestion: An update reaches one instance and others serve stale data for minutes. How do you invalidate?
modules.learningDelta: Coherence requires invalidation or versioning across every cache layer; pub/sub is fast but lossy, so TTLs remain a backstop

modules.title: Cache Penetration: Requests for Missing Keys
modules.purpose: Stop misses for nonexistent keys from reaching the database
modules.productionQuestion: Random IDs miss the cache and hit the database every time. What do you add?
modules.learningDelta: Penetration is repeated lookup of absent keys; negative caching and Bloom filters reject impossible keys early

modules.title: Negative Caching and Bloom Filters
modules.purpose: Reject impossible keys before the database
modules.productionQuestion: A scraper requests 10k random IDs per second. How do you protect the database?
modules.learningDelta: Negative caching stores absence with a short TTL; Bloom filters reject definitely-absent keys with a tunable false-positive rate

modules.title: Redis Cluster Resharding: MOVED and ASK
modules.purpose: Move slots without breaking clients
modules.productionQuestion: During a reshard, some clients receive MOVED and others time out. What is happening?
modules.learningDelta: Redis Cluster redirects keys with MOVED and ASK during migration; clients must follow redirects and handle transient failures

modules.title: Redis vs Memcached
modules.purpose: Choose a cache for the access pattern, not the benchmark
modules.productionQuestion: You need sorted sets, persistence, and pub/sub. Is Memcached simpler and faster enough?
modules.learningDelta: Memcached is a simple multithreaded cache; Redis adds data structures, persistence, replication, and cluster semantics at operational cost

modules.title: Cache-Aside vs Write-Through
modules.purpose: Keep reads fast without losing write durability
modules.productionQuestion: Writes must be durable and reads must be fast. Where does the cache sit?
modules.learningDelta: Cache-aside leaves the cache optional and can serve stale data; write-through keeps it fresh but adds write latency and failure coupling

modules.title: Write-Behind: Speed With a Data-Loss Window
modules.purpose: Decide whether asynchronous writes are acceptable
modules.productionQuestion: Write-behind makes writes 10× faster, but the cache crashes. What is lost?
modules.learningDelta: Write-behind acknowledges before durable storage, creating a loss window and ordering complexity

modules.title: Big Keys: One Key, Many Problems
modules.purpose: Find and split keys that block the event loop
modules.productionQuestion: Redis latency spikes every time a 50MB key is read. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Big keys consume bandwidth, block the single-threaded event loop during operations, and create uneven shard memory

modules.title: Slow Commands and the Redis Event Loop
modules.purpose: Protect the single-threaded data path
modules.productionQuestion: Redis p99 spikes on every `KEYS *` call from a debug script. What is the mechanism?
modules.learningDelta: Redis executes commands on one thread per shard; O(N) commands and large values delay every other client

modules.title: Lua Scripts: Atomicity and Blocking
modules.purpose: Use atomic scripts without creating a new stall
modules.productionQuestion: A Lua script fixes a race but raises p99. What is the risk?
modules.learningDelta: Lua runs atomically on the server and blocks other commands; long scripts turn correctness fixes into latency incidents

modules.title: Redis Connection Pool Exhaustion
modules.purpose: Size pools for concurrency, not for comfort
modules.productionQuestion: Services time out waiting for a Redis connection while Redis CPU is low. What is the bottleneck?
modules.learningDelta: Pool exhaustion is a local queueing problem; too few connections wait, too many multiply sessions and failover churn

modules.title: Local Cache Bypass on ECS
modules.purpose: Make a local cache safe across deployments and tasks
modules.productionQuestion: A local cache speeds reads but a bad value cannot be purged. What escape hatch do you need?
modules.learningDelta: Local caches need a bypass, versioning, or kill switch so operators can recover without redeploying every task

modules.title: Redis Memory Fragmentation
modules.purpose: Distinguish used memory from resident memory
modules.productionQuestion: Redis used_memory is 6GB but the process uses 10GB and the host is OOMing. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Allocator fragmentation, peak memory, and replica buffers make RSS larger than the logical dataset; fragmentation ratio explains the gap

modules.title: Cache Warming After a Cold Start
modules.purpose: Refill a cache without melting the database
modules.productionQuestion: A Redis restart leaves an empty cache and the database is overwhelmed. How do you warm it?
modules.learningDelta: Cold caches shift load to the origin; controlled warming, request coalescing, and rate limits prevent a restart from becoming an outage

modules.title: Redis Cluster Failover
modules.purpose: Keep reads and writes correct when a shard fails over
modules.productionQuestion: A primary fails over and clients see a burst of errors. What does the cluster guarantee?
modules.learningDelta: Redis Cluster promotes a replica after failure detection; clients must refresh topology, retry safely, and tolerate a short write outage

modules.title: RDS and Aurora Architecture
modules.purpose: Place the writer, readers, storage, and endpoints correctly
modules.productionQuestion: A read query is hitting the writer and piling up locks. Which endpoint and topology should it use?
modules.learningDelta: RDS and Aurora separate compute from storage differently; endpoints and replicas determine where reads and writes go

modules.title: Replication Lag: Measure It Before You Trust It
modules.purpose: Detect lag that a healthy dashboard hides
modules.productionQuestion: The replica is healthy but users see stale data. Which lag metric do you trust?
modules.learningDelta: Replication lag is both time and byte based; a replica can be current in bytes yet slow to apply, and vice versa

modules.title: Read Replica Routing Without Stale Reads
modules.purpose: Send reads to replicas only when the product allows it
modules.productionQuestion: A user updates a profile and immediately reads an old value from a replica. How do you route?
modules.learningDelta: Read routing must respect read-your-writes; sticky-to-primary windows, session consistency, or write-through caches solve different cases

modules.title: Aurora Global Database
modules.purpose: Reason about cross-region reads and failover
modules.productionQuestion: You need a secondary region for disaster recovery and local reads. What does Aurora Global Database replicate?
modules.learningDelta: Aurora Global Database replicates storage asynchronously to secondary regions; read replicas serve local reads and promotion changes the writer

modules.title: Cross-Region Lag and RPO
modules.purpose: Decide whether a regional failover is safe
modules.productionQuestion: The primary region is failing and replica lag is 90 seconds. How much data do you lose on promotion?
modules.learningDelta: RPO is bounded by replication lag at failover; promotion discards unreplicated writes and requires application reconciliation

modules.title: Aurora Write Forwarding
modules.purpose: Route writes from a secondary without stale reads
modules.productionQuestion: A secondary-region app needs writes but must not send them to a stale local writer. What does write forwarding do?
modules.learningDelta: Write forwarding sends writes from a secondary cluster to the primary writer, adding latency and preserving a single writer

modules.title: PgBouncer: Pool Before the Database
modules.purpose: Reduce database connections without breaking session state
modules.productionQuestion: 200 app tasks each open 20 connections and the database refuses new ones. How do you pool?
modules.learningDelta: PgBouncer multiplexes client connections onto fewer server connections; transaction pooling breaks session-level features

modules.title: RDS Proxy: Managed Pooling and Failover
modules.purpose: Keep connections alive through failover
modules.productionQuestion: A database failover causes a connection storm and a long outage. How does RDS Proxy change it?
modules.learningDelta: RDS Proxy pools and holds connections, masking failover from clients, but adds a hop and has its own limits

modules.title: Max Connections: The Limit Behind the Limit
modules.purpose: Size connections from memory and concurrency
modules.productionQuestion: The database has 500 max connections but dies at 300. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Each connection consumes memory and workers; the practical limit is lower than max_connections and depends on workload

modules.title: Read-After-Write Consistency
modules.purpose: Keep a user's own writes visible
modules.productionQuestion: A user saves a setting and the next page load shows the old value. How do you fix it without going back to the primary for everything?
modules.learningDelta: Read-after-write requires routing the user's reads to a consistent source for a window, or propagating a version token

modules.title: Database Failover and DNS
modules.purpose: Understand why clients keep hitting the old writer
modules.productionQuestion: The database failed over but the app still writes to the old primary. What did DNS do?
modules.learningDelta: Managed failover updates a DNS name, but client caches, connection pools, and TTLs determine how fast traffic moves

modules.title: Split Brain: Two Writers, One Truth
modules.purpose: Prevent divergent writes during a partition
modules.productionQuestion: Two database nodes both accept writes during a network partition. How do you recover?
modules.learningDelta: Split brain requires fencing, quorum, or a single-writer design; reconciliation after divergence is expensive and sometimes impossible

modules.title: Backups and Point-in-Time Recovery
modules.purpose: Recover to the right second, not just the last backup
modules.productionQuestion: A bad migration deletes rows at 14:07. How do you restore without losing 14:00–14:07?
modules.learningDelta: PITR combines a base backup with continuous logs; recovery point and restore time are different objectives

modules.title: DR Drills: Prove RTO and RPO
modules.purpose: Test recovery before the real incident
modules.productionQuestion: The DR plan says 15 minutes RTO. Has anyone measured it?
modules.learningDelta: Untested recovery is a hypothesis; drills measure restore time, data loss, DNS cutover, and application readiness

modules.title: Vacuum and Bloat
modules.purpose: Reclaim space without locking the table
modules.productionQuestion: A table grows despite deletes and queries slow down. What is bloat doing?
modules.learningDelta: PostgreSQL MVCC keeps dead tuples until vacuum; bloat increases I/O and can make plans worse, while aggressive vacuum competes for resources

modules.title: Locks and Deadlocks
modules.purpose: Find the transaction holding the lock
modules.productionQuestion: Writes hang and the database reports deadlocks. Which query do you inspect first?
modules.learningDelta: Lock waits and deadlocks come from transaction ordering; pg_locks and wait events reveal the blocker, but killing it has consequences

modules.title: Long Transactions: Locks, Bloat, and Lag
modules.purpose: Bound transaction duration before it causes an outage
modules.productionQuestion: A reporting query runs for 40 minutes and replication lag climbs. What is the chain?
modules.learningDelta: Long transactions hold snapshots and locks, delay vacuum, and can block replication; they turn a read into a system-wide problem

modules.title: Indexing: The Right Index for the Query
modules.purpose: Add an index without making writes worse
modules.productionQuestion: A query is slow and adding an index doubles write latency. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: Indexes trade read speed for write cost and space; the query plan, selectivity, and column order decide whether an index helps

modules.title: Query Plans: Why the Index Is Ignored
modules.purpose: Read a plan before changing a query
modules.productionQuestion: An index exists but the planner chooses a sequential scan. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Plans depend on statistics, selectivity, cost, and predicates; stale stats or functions on columns defeat indexes

modules.title: N+1 Queries: Count the Round Trips
modules.purpose: Find the query pattern that multiplies latency
modules.productionQuestion: A page loads 200 items and makes 201 queries. Where do you fix it?
modules.learningDelta: N+1 comes from per-item queries; batching, joins, or dataloaders reduce round trips and connection pressure

modules.title: Partitioning and Sharding
modules.purpose: Split data without breaking queries
modules.productionQuestion: A table is too large for one writer. Do you partition, shard, or archive?
modules.learningDelta: Partitioning splits one logical table for maintenance; sharding splits writers across nodes and adds routing and cross-shard complexity

modules.title: Hot Partitions
modules.purpose: Find the partition taking most of the traffic
modules.productionQuestion: One tenant's partition receives 60% of writes and its disk is full. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: A hot partition is a data-distribution problem; splitting the key or isolating the tenant changes the balance and the operational model

modules.title: Multi-AZ vs Multi-Region
modules.purpose: Choose a failure domain and be honest about RTO
modules.productionQuestion: The business needs 99.99% and 15-minute RTO. Is Multi-AZ enough?
modules.learningDelta: Multi-AZ protects against an AZ failure with a synchronous standby; multi-region protects against a region failure with asynchronous lag and higher RTO

modules.title: Cross-AZ Latency and Cost
modules.purpose: Keep chatty database traffic inside a zone
modules.productionQuestion: The database bill includes a large cross-AZ transfer line. Why is the app talking across zones?
modules.learningDelta: Cross-AZ traffic adds latency and cost; reader placement, chatty queries, and retry loops multiply it

modules.title: Aurora Serverless Scaling
modules.purpose: Understand cold starts and capacity units
modules.productionQuestion: A serverless database is slow after idle periods. What is happening?
modules.learningDelta: Aurora Serverless scales capacity in units and may need to resume; pooling, min capacity, and warm traffic change the experience

modules.title: Parameter Groups: Change With a Plan
modules.purpose: Apply database settings without a surprise restart
modules.productionQuestion: A parameter change improves one query and breaks another. How do you roll it out?
modules.learningDelta: Parameter groups apply engine settings; some are dynamic, some require reboot, and cluster-level settings have different scope

modules.title: Storage Autoscaling
modules.purpose: Avoid a full disk without unbounded growth
modules.productionQuestion: Disk usage climbs and autoscaling has a maximum. What happens at the cap?
modules.learningDelta: Storage autoscaling adds capacity within a maximum; growth rate, retention, and temporary files determine whether it saves you

modules.title: Replication Thread Bottlenecks
modules.purpose: Find why a replica cannot keep up
modules.productionQuestion: Replica CPU is low but lag grows during a write burst. Which resource is the bottleneck?
modules.learningDelta: Replication apply is often single-threaded or limited by I/O; more replicas do not fix a slow apply path

modules.title: Connection Storms After Failover
modules.purpose: Prevent every client from reconnecting at once
modules.productionQuestion: A failover triggers 10k reconnects and the new writer is overwhelmed. How do you dampen it?
modules.learningDelta: Reconnect storms need jitter, backoff, connection pooling, and pre-warmed capacity; immediate retries amplify the failover

modules.title: Cold Read Replicas
modules.purpose: Understand why a new replica is slow
modules.productionQuestion: You add a read replica during an incident and it makes latency worse. Why?
modules.learningDelta: A new replica must catch up and warm its cache; reads routed too early hit cold storage and increase lag

modules.title: Aurora Backtrack
modules.purpose: Rewind a cluster without a full restore
modules.productionQuestion: A bad migration changed data 20 minutes ago. Can you rewind instead of restoring?
modules.learningDelta: Aurora Backtrack rewinds cluster state within a retention window, but it is not a substitute for backups and has limits

modules.title: Connection Leaks
modules.purpose: Find the code path that never returns a connection
modules.productionQuestion: The pool is exhausted but request rate is normal. Where did the connections go?
modules.learningDelta: A connection leak holds a session after an error path; pool metrics and stack traces reveal it, but only if timeouts and close paths are correct

modules.title: MongoDB Replica Sets
modules.purpose: Explain primary, secondaries, and elections
modules.productionQuestion: The primary disappears and the app reconnects to a new node. What happened underneath?
modules.learningDelta: A replica set elects one primary; secondaries apply the oplog, and clients discover topology changes

modules.title: Read Preference
modules.purpose: Route reads without breaking the product's freshness needs
modules.productionQuestion: A dashboard reads from a lagging secondary and shows old data. Which read preference fits?
modules.learningDelta: Read preference trades freshness for locality and load; primary, primaryPreferred, secondary, and nearest have different failure behavior

modules.title: Write Concern
modules.purpose: Choose durability and latency deliberately
modules.productionQuestion: A write is acknowledged and then lost after a primary crash. What write concern was used?
modules.learningDelta: Write concern controls how many nodes acknowledge before success; w:1 is fast but can lose writes on failover

modules.title: Adding Readers During an Incident
modules.purpose: Avoid making an incident worse with a new secondary
modules.productionQuestion: The primary is overloaded, so you add a secondary. Why did latency get worse?
modules.learningDelta: A new secondary performs an initial sync and then serves cold reads; it increases primary load and replication pressure before it helps

modules.title: Cold Secondaries
modules.purpose: Understand the cache cost of a new replica
modules.productionQuestion: A secondary has low CPU but serves reads slowly. Why?
modules.learningDelta: A new secondary has a cold WiredTiger cache; serving reads before it warms up increases disk I/O and latency

modules.title: Replication Lag and the Oplog
modules.purpose: Detect a secondary that cannot keep up
modules.productionQuestion: Replica lag grows during a write burst and then the secondary falls off the oplog. What happens?
modules.learningDelta: Secondaries apply the capped oplog; if they fall behind the window they need a full resync, not a quick catch-up

modules.title: Elections and Availability
modules.purpose: Explain why writes fail briefly during failover
modules.productionQuestion: The primary failed and writes failed for 12 seconds. What determines that window?
modules.learningDelta: Elections require a majority and take time; electionTimeout, heartbeat, and catch-up determine write availability

modules.title: Sharding Architecture
modules.purpose: Place mongos, config servers, and shards correctly
modules.productionQuestion: A sharded cluster routes queries slowly. Which component is involved?
modules.learningDelta: mongos routes queries using config server metadata; shards hold data, and routing decisions depend on the shard key

modules.title: Shard Key Design
modules.purpose: Choose a key that distributes writes and supports queries
modules.productionQuestion: One shard key gives perfect distribution but every query is scatter-gather. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Shard keys must balance write distribution and query locality; high cardinality alone is not enough

modules.title: Hot Shards
modules.purpose: Find the shard taking disproportionate writes
modules.productionQuestion: One shard has 80% CPU and the others are idle. Is the balancer broken?
modules.learningDelta: The balancer moves chunks, but a hot key within a chunk or a monotonically increasing key can keep one shard hot

modules.title: Chunk Migration
modules.purpose: Move data without hurting latency
modules.productionQuestion: The balancer starts migrating chunks and p99 rises. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Chunk migration copies data and updates metadata; it consumes I/O and network and can compete with application traffic

modules.title: The Balancer
modules.purpose: Decide when balancing helps and when it hurts
modules.productionQuestion: Chunks are imbalanced but the balancer is off. Should you turn it on during peak?
modules.learningDelta: The balancer improves distribution over time but adds load; windows and thresholds determine whether it helps during an incident

modules.title: Connection Storms
modules.purpose: Protect mongos and shards from reconnect waves
modules.productionQuestion: A network blip causes every app worker to reconnect and mongos CPU spikes. How do you dampen it?
modules.learningDelta: MongoDB drivers pool connections; synchronized reconnects overwhelm mongos and shards without backoff and pool limits

modules.title: Index Design
modules.purpose: Build compound indexes that match query shapes
modules.productionQuestion: A compound index is not used even though its fields appear in the query. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Index field order, sort direction, and predicate shape determine whether MongoDB can use an index efficiently

modules.title: Aggregation Pipeline Performance
modules.purpose: Push filters and limits before the expensive stages
modules.productionQuestion: An aggregation pipeline is slow even with an index. Where is the work happening?
modules.learningDelta: Pipeline stage order determines whether indexes, memory, and disk are used; early filters and limits reduce work

modules.title: Change Streams
modules.purpose: React to writes without polling the collection
modules.productionQuestion: A downstream service polls MongoDB every second and adds load. Can it subscribe instead?
modules.learningDelta: Change streams expose a resumable oplog cursor; resume tokens and majority read concern determine durability and replay

modules.title: Retryable Writes
modules.purpose: Make transient failover errors safe to retry
modules.productionQuestion: A write fails during failover and the driver retries it. Could it apply twice?
modules.learningDelta: Retryable writes use a session and transaction number so the server can deduplicate retries within a window

modules.title: Transactions and Their Limits
modules.purpose: Use multi-document transactions when the boundary is real
modules.productionQuestion: A transaction spans 10 minutes and 50k documents. What breaks first?
modules.learningDelta: MongoDB transactions have time and size limits and hold resources; they are not a substitute for schema design

modules.title: Backup and Restore
modules.purpose: Recover a replica set or sharded cluster coherently
modules.productionQuestion: A restore of one shard completes but the cluster is inconsistent. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Cluster-consistent backups require coordination across shards and config servers; restoring one node is not a cluster restore

modules.title: Write Amplification
modules.purpose: See why one write costs many I/O operations
modules.productionQuestion: Write throughput drops and disk I/O is saturated. What is write amplification doing?
modules.learningDelta: Indexes, journaling, replication, and document growth multiply physical writes; more indexes can hurt write capacity

modules.title: Read Concern
modules.purpose: Choose the consistency of a read
modules.productionQuestion: A read returns data that is later rolled back. Which read concern was used?
modules.learningDelta: Read concern controls the visibility and durability of reads; local can return data not yet majority-committed

modules.title: Mongos Routing and Targets
modules.purpose: Diagnose a slow query across a sharded cluster
modules.productionQuestion: A query is slow only when it goes through mongos. What do you inspect?
modules.learningDelta: Mongos routes by shard key, merges results, and applies targeting; scatter-gather and merge overhead can dominate

modules.title: Kafka Partitions: The Unit of Parallelism
modules.purpose: Reason about ordering, throughput, and consumer scaling
modules.productionQuestion: A topic has 12 partitions and 20 consumers. Why are 8 consumers idle?
modules.learningDelta: A partition is consumed by one consumer per group; partition count caps consumer parallelism and sets ordering scope

modules.title: Keys and Ordering
modules.purpose: Keep per-entity order without global serialization
modules.productionQuestion: Two updates for one order arrive out of order. What key should the producer use?
modules.learningDelta: Kafka preserves order within a partition; keying by entity keeps its events ordered while allowing parallelism across keys

modules.title: Consumer Groups and Offsets
modules.purpose: Understand lag, commits, and replay
modules.productionQuestion: A consumer restarts and reprocesses 10 minutes of events. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Offsets are committed by the group; commit interval and processing semantics determine replay and duplicates

modules.title: Rebalancing: Stop the World
modules.purpose: Reduce consumer pauses during scaling and failure
modules.productionQuestion: Adding one consumer pauses the whole group for 40 seconds. What causes the pause?
modules.learningDelta: Rebalances revoke and reassign partitions; eager protocols pause all consumers, cooperative protocols reduce the blast radius

modules.title: Kafka Hot Partition
modules.purpose: Spread one key that dominates a topic
modules.productionQuestion: One partition is at 100% and the others are idle because one key is 60% of traffic. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Hot partitions come from key skew; salting, key redesign, or splitting the event changes ordering and consumer logic

modules.title: Partition Count: More Is Not Free
modules.purpose: Choose a partition count for throughput and recovery
modules.productionQuestion: The topic has 200 partitions and failover takes minutes. What did the partition count cost?
modules.learningDelta: More partitions add parallelism but increase metadata, rebalance time, file handles, and end-to-end latency

modules.title: Retention and Replay
modules.purpose: Keep enough history to recover without unbounded cost
modules.productionQuestion: A consumer is down for two days and retention is 24 hours. What happens?
modules.learningDelta: Retention bounds replay; time and size limits delete segments, and a consumer beyond the window loses data

modules.title: Producer Acks
modules.purpose: Choose durability versus latency
modules.productionQuestion: A producer returns success and the broker loses the event. What acks setting was used?
modules.learningDelta: acks=0/1/all trade latency for durability; acks=all with min.insync.replicas is required for strong guarantees

modules.title: Idempotent Producer
modules.purpose: Stop retries from duplicating events
modules.productionQuestion: A producer retries a batch and the consumer sees duplicates. What fixes it?
modules.learningDelta: Idempotent producers use sequence numbers and producer IDs to deduplicate retries within a session

modules.title: Backpressure in Streaming
modules.purpose: Keep a fast producer from overwhelming consumers
modules.productionQuestion: The producer outruns consumers and lag grows without bound. Where do you apply backpressure?
modules.learningDelta: Backpressure can throttle producers, buffer durably in the log, or shed work; the log is not infinite and lag is a debt

modules.title: Consumer Lag: The Real SLO
modules.purpose: Alert on time-to-catch-up, not just message count
modules.productionQuestion: Consumer lag is 2 million messages. Is that bad?
modules.learningDelta: Lag must be interpreted with production rate and processing rate; time-to-catch-up is the user-facing signal

modules.title: Slow Consumers
modules.purpose: Find why one consumer holds back a partition
modules.productionQuestion: One consumer processes 10× slower than its peers. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: Per-partition processing time, downstream calls, and poison records identify slow consumers; more consumers cannot split one partition

modules.title: Poison Messages
modules.purpose: Stop one bad record from blocking a partition
modules.productionQuestion: One malformed event fails every retry and the partition stops. How do you recover?
modules.learningDelta: A poison message blocks in-order processing; validation, retry limits, and DLQs isolate it without losing the stream

modules.title: Dead Letter Queues
modules.purpose: Isolate failures without hiding them
modules.productionQuestion: Failed events go to a DLQ and no one notices for a week. What is missing?
modules.learningDelta: A DLQ is only useful with replay, alerting, ownership, and a retention policy; otherwise it becomes a data dump

modules.title: Exactly-Once Semantics
modules.purpose: Separate broker guarantees from end-to-end effects
modules.productionQuestion: Kafka is configured for exactly-once, but the sink still has duplicates. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Kafka transactions make broker writes atomic; end-to-end exactly-once requires idempotent sinks or transactional outputs

modules.title: Kafka Transactions
modules.purpose: Group writes and offsets atomically
modules.productionQuestion: A consumer writes output and commits its offset separately, causing duplicates. How do transactions help?
modules.learningDelta: Transactions atomically commit produced records and consumed offsets, but add latency and require transactional consumers

modules.title: Confluent Cloud Operations
modules.purpose: Diagnose cluster limits and networking
modules.productionQuestion: A managed Kafka cluster shows elevated latency and the app team cannot see brokers. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: Managed Kafka exposes throughput, partition, and network limits through metrics and quotas; the broker is not yours to tune

modules.title: Schema Registry and Compatibility
modules.purpose: Evolve events without breaking consumers
modules.productionQuestion: A producer adds a required field and old consumers crash. What compatibility mode?
modules.learningDelta: Schema compatibility modes govern evolution; backward, forward, and full compatibility have different deploy orders

modules.title: ksqlDB Queries and State
modules.purpose: Understand state stores and reprocessing
modules.productionQuestion: A ksqlDB query restarts and takes 20 minutes to catch up. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Stateful queries rebuild state stores from the changelog; restart time depends on state size and changelog throughput

modules.title: WarpStream on Object Storage
modules.purpose: Reason about Kafka-compatible streaming on S3
modules.productionQuestion: A Kafka-compatible service stores data in object storage. What changes for latency and cost?
modules.learningDelta: Object-storage streaming trades broker-local disk for S3 latency and cost; tail latency and metadata operations dominate

modules.title: Object-Storage Streaming Latency
modules.purpose: Separate throughput from tail latency
modules.productionQuestion: Object storage delivers high throughput but p99 reads are slow. Which workload is affected?
modules.learningDelta: Object storage favors throughput and durability; per-request latency and metadata operations make it unsuitable for some low-latency paths

modules.title: MQTT QoS 0, 1, and 2
modules.purpose: Choose delivery semantics for constrained devices
modules.productionQuestion: A sensor publishes telemetry and the broker restarts. Which QoS prevents loss?
modules.learningDelta: QoS 0 is fire-and-forget, QoS 1 is at-least-once, QoS 2 is exactly-once at the protocol level with higher overhead

modules.title: MQTT Retained Messages
modules.purpose: Give new subscribers the current state
modules.productionQuestion: A dashboard reconnects and shows no values until the next publish. What do you enable?
modules.learningDelta: Retained messages store the last value per topic and deliver it on subscribe, trading broker state for freshness

modules.title: MQTT Fan-Out
modules.purpose: Scale many subscribers per topic
modules.productionQuestion: One telemetry topic has 50k subscribers and the broker is overloaded. How do you fan out?
modules.learningDelta: MQTT fan-out is broker-bound; shared subscriptions, topic trees, and bridging distribute subscribers across brokers

modules.title: MQTT Broker Scaling
modules.purpose: Add brokers without losing session state
modules.productionQuestion: You add a broker and existing clients lose their sessions. Why?
modules.learningDelta: MQTT sessions and retained state are broker-local unless clustered or bridged; scaling requires state strategy

modules.title: SQS Visibility Timeout
modules.purpose: Prevent duplicate processing and stuck messages
modules.productionQuestion: A consumer takes longer than the visibility timeout and the message is processed twice. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Visibility timeout hides a message while it is processed; it must exceed processing time or be extended, and failures need a DLQ

modules.title: SQS FIFO
modules.purpose: Get ordering without a single consumer
modules.productionQuestion: You need per-customer order and high throughput. How does FIFO scale?
modules.learningDelta: FIFO queues preserve order within a message group; throughput scales with groups, and a hot group serializes

modules.title: SNS and EventBridge Routing
modules.purpose: Fan out notifications and route events without hidden coupling
modules.productionQuestion: A notification goes to five subscribers and a new event triggers three unintended consumers. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: SNS fan-out and EventBridge rules solve different routing problems; broad patterns and shared buses create hidden consumers and ordering surprises

modules.title: Transactional Outbox
modules.purpose: Publish events without dual-write failures
modules.productionQuestion: The database commit succeeds and the Kafka publish fails. How do you keep them consistent?
modules.learningDelta: The outbox pattern writes the event in the same transaction and publishes it asynchronously, using polling or CDC

modules.title: Change Data Capture
modules.purpose: Stream database changes without polling
modules.productionQuestion: A downstream index lags by an hour because it polls the database. Can CDC help?
modules.learningDelta: CDC reads the database log and emits ordered changes; snapshotting, schema changes, and tombstones add complexity

modules.title: Queue Depth vs Latency
modules.purpose: Use the right backlog signal
modules.productionQuestion: Queue depth is 10k but latency is fine; another queue has depth 100 and is timing out. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Queue depth alone is ambiguous; arrival rate, service rate, and age of oldest message determine user impact

modules.title: Kafka ISR and Under-Replicated Partitions
modules.purpose: Detect durability risk before a broker loss
modules.productionQuestion: One broker is down and partitions are under-replicated. Are writes still safe?
modules.learningDelta: ISR tracks in-sync replicas; min.insync.replicas and acks determine whether writes continue and whether durability is reduced

modules.title: ECS Task Definitions
modules.purpose: Understand the immutable unit of deployment
modules.productionQuestion: A task restarts with different environment variables than the last run. Where do you look?
modules.learningDelta: A task definition is an immutable revision of image, CPU, memory, env, volumes, and IAM; services pin a revision

modules.title: ECS Services and Desired Count
modules.purpose: Reconcile desired state with reality
modules.productionQuestion: The service says 10 tasks desired but only 6 are running. What does ECS do next?
modules.learningDelta: A service continuously reconciles desired count with running tasks through the scheduler and deployment configuration

modules.title: ECS Placement
modules.purpose: Spread tasks without breaking capacity
modules.productionQuestion: All tasks land on one container instance and it saturates. How do you spread them?
modules.learningDelta: Placement strategies and constraints control bin packing and spread; Fargate abstracts instances but not AZ spread

modules.title: Target Tracking Scaling
modules.purpose: Scale on the signal that actually predicts load
