modules.productionQuestion: CPU stays at 40% while latency rises and the service does not scale. What metric should drive scaling?
modules.learningDelta: Target tracking follows a metric and a target; choosing CPU when the bottleneck is queue depth or concurrency causes late scaling

modules.title: Step Scaling
modules.purpose: React to thresholds without oscillating
modules.productionQuestion: Traffic crosses a threshold repeatedly and the service flaps between 4 and 20 tasks. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Step scaling uses thresholds and cooldowns; missing scale-in stabilization causes oscillation and cold starts

modules.title: Scaling Cooldowns and Stabilization
modules.purpose: Avoid scaling on noise
modules.productionQuestion: A one-minute spike triggers 30 tasks and then they all scale in. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Cooldowns and stabilization windows filter noise but delay response; the right values depend on workload duration

modules.title: ECS Deployment Circuit Breaker
modules.purpose: Roll back a bad deployment automatically
modules.productionQuestion: A new task revision fails health checks and the deployment hangs. How do you make ECS roll back?
modules.learningDelta: The deployment circuit breaker detects repeated task failures and can roll back automatically when configured

modules.title: ECS Rolling Deployments
modules.purpose: Keep capacity during rollout
modules.productionQuestion: A rolling deployment drops below the minimum healthy percent and causes 503s. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: minimumHealthyPercent and maximumPercent control rolling capacity; task draining and health checks determine actual availability

modules.title: Fargate Cold Starts
modules.purpose: Account for time before a task serves traffic
modules.productionQuestion: Autoscaling adds tasks but p99 still spikes for two minutes. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Fargate tasks need scheduling, image pull, startup, and health check time before serving; scaling must anticipate it

modules.title: Image Pull and Registry Limits
modules.purpose: Stop deployments from stalling on image pulls
modules.productionQuestion: New tasks take 90 seconds to start and the registry is throttling. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Image size, layers, cache, and registry pull limits determine task startup; a large image multiplies cold-start cost

modules.title: ALB Target Registration for ECS
modules.purpose: Get tasks into the target group reliably
modules.productionQuestion: A task is running but receives no traffic. What registration state do you check?
modules.learningDelta: ECS registers tasks by IP or instance; target group health, security groups, and ports decide traffic

modules.title: Task Draining
modules.purpose: Remove tasks without cutting requests
modules.productionQuestion: A deployment causes 502s during task stop. What is the drain sequence?
modules.learningDelta: ECS deregisters a task, waits for draining, then stops it; timeout and connection behavior decide in-flight request loss

modules.title: ECS Exec
modules.purpose: Debug a live task without SSH
modules.productionQuestion: A task is unhealthy but you cannot shell in. How do you inspect it?
modules.learningDelta: ECS Exec uses SSM to run commands in a running task; it requires task role, SSM agent, and audit controls

modules.title: ECS Logs
modules.purpose: Find logs after a task disappears
modules.productionQuestion: A task was OOM-killed and its container is gone. Where are the logs?
modules.learningDelta: ECS log drivers ship stdout/stderr to CloudWatch or FireLens; task stop reason and previous logs are separate signals

modules.title: Container Health Checks
modules.purpose: Distinguish liveness from readiness
modules.productionQuestion: A task is healthy but not ready, or ready but dead. Which check do you fix?
modules.learningDelta: Container and load balancer health checks answer different questions; liveness restarts, readiness removes traffic

modules.title: Service Discovery
modules.purpose: Resolve services without hard-coded IPs
modules.productionQuestion: A service calls another by IP and a task replacement breaks it. What do you use?
modules.learningDelta: Service discovery maps stable names to changing task IPs; DNS TTL and health determine failover

modules.title: Cloud Map
modules.purpose: Register and discover ECS services
modules.productionQuestion: You need private DNS for 40 services. How does Cloud Map work?
modules.learningDelta: Cloud Map maintains namespaces and service instances; health checks and TTLs control resolution and failover

modules.title: CPU and Memory Limits
modules.purpose: Prevent one task from starving its neighbors
modules.productionQuestion: One task uses all node memory and other tasks are evicted. How do limits work?
modules.learningDelta: Container and task limits bound CPU and memory; reservations influence placement, and exceeding memory leads to OOM

modules.title: OOM Kills
modules.purpose: Find what consumed memory before the kill
modules.productionQuestion: A task restarts with exit code 137. Was it CPU throttling or memory?
modules.learningDelta: Exit 137 is SIGKILL; OOM kills leave a stop reason and memory metrics, while CPU throttling does not kill

modules.title: Task IAM Roles
modules.purpose: Give tasks least privilege without static keys
modules.productionQuestion: A task needs S3 access but the node role can read everything. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Task roles are per-task credentials delivered by the agent; execution roles are separate and used to pull images and write logs

modules.title: Secrets in ECS
modules.purpose: Inject secrets without baking them into images
modules.productionQuestion: A database password is in an environment variable in the task definition. What is the safer path?
modules.learningDelta: Secrets Manager or SSM parameters can be injected at task start; image, task definition, and logs must stay free of secrets

modules.title: Capacity Providers
modules.purpose: Mix Fargate and EC2 without surprises
modules.productionQuestion: A service moves to a capacity provider and tasks fail to place. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Capacity providers define capacity and strategy; weights, base, and instance types determine placement and cost

modules.title: Multi-AZ Scheduling
modules.purpose: Spread tasks across zones
modules.productionQuestion: One AZ loses a node and too many tasks were packed there. How do you spread them?
modules.learningDelta: The scheduler places tasks across zones, but capacity and placement constraints can concentrate them

modules.title: Batch vs Service
modules.purpose: Choose the right ECS scheduler
modules.productionQuestion: A nightly job runs as a service and restarts forever. What should it be?
modules.learningDelta: Services maintain desired count; batch jobs run to completion and retry differently, with different observability

modules.title: Sidecar Patterns
modules.purpose: Add logging, proxy, or security without breaking tasks
modules.productionQuestion: A sidecar doubles task CPU and the service is throttled. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: Sidecars share task resources; CPU/memory limits and startup order affect the main container

modules.title: Fargate Spot
modules.purpose: Use interruption-tolerant capacity
modules.productionQuestion: Fargate Spot is cheaper but tasks disappear. Which workloads fit?
modules.learningDelta: Fargate Spot uses spare capacity with interruption notices; stateless, retryable, and drained workloads tolerate it

modules.title: Envoy Listeners
modules.purpose: Understand where traffic enters the proxy
modules.productionQuestion: A request never reaches the service. Which Envoy listener should have accepted it?
modules.learningDelta: Envoy listeners bind addresses and ports and pass connections into filter chains and route configuration

modules.title: Envoy Clusters and Endpoints
modules.purpose: See how the proxy chooses a backend
modules.productionQuestion: The mesh reports no healthy upstreams while pods are running. Which cluster view do you check?
modules.learningDelta: Envoy clusters group endpoints and health; outlier ejection and endpoint discovery determine usable capacity

modules.title: Envoy Routes
modules.purpose: Route by host, path, and header without surprises
modules.productionQuestion: A canary route works for one header but all traffic hits the stable version. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Routes match in order; host/path/header predicates and route order decide which cluster receives traffic

modules.title: Kuma Control Plane
modules.purpose: Separate data plane behavior from control plane policy
modules.productionQuestion: A policy applies to half the mesh and no one knows why. Where is the selector?
modules.learningDelta: Kuma's control plane distributes policies to selected data plane proxies; selectors, mesh scope, and versions decide where they apply

modules.title: mTLS in the Mesh
modules.purpose: Encrypt and authenticate service traffic
modules.productionQuestion: A service accepts plaintext from inside the mesh. What policy prevents it?
modules.learningDelta: mTLS authenticates both sides with certificates; permissive mode allows plaintext and hides misconfiguration

modules.title: Mesh Retries
modules.purpose: Retry safely at the proxy layer
modules.productionQuestion: Envoy retries every 503 three times and the dependency collapses. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Proxy retries are powerful and dangerous; retry budgets, conditions, and per-try timeout prevent amplification

modules.title: Mesh Timeouts
modules.purpose: Set deadlines at the right layer
modules.productionQuestion: The proxy returns 504 before the service finishes. Which timeout won?
modules.learningDelta: Proxy timeout, route timeout, and application deadline are separate; the smallest wins and retries can stack

modules.title: Mesh Circuit Breaking
modules.purpose: Shed load before the dependency fails
modules.productionQuestion: A dependency is slow and Envoy keeps opening new connections. What limits do you set?
modules.learningDelta: Envoy circuit breakers cap connections, pending requests, and retries; they protect the upstream and fail fast locally

modules.title: Outlier Detection
modules.purpose: Eject bad endpoints without ejecting the fleet
modules.productionQuestion: One pod returns errors and Envoy ejects healthy pods too. What threshold is wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Outlier detection ejects hosts based on consecutive errors and ejection percentage; overly aggressive settings remove capacity

modules.title: Traffic Splitting
modules.purpose: Shift traffic without changing clients
modules.productionQuestion: You need 5% canary traffic and instant rollback. Where do you implement it?
modules.learningDelta: Mesh traffic splitting weights clusters by route; it is fast to change but must align with observability and health

modules.title: Canary Through the Mesh
modules.purpose: Gate a rollout on real signals
modules.productionQuestion: The canary has 5% traffic and no errors; can you increase to 100%?
modules.learningDelta: A canary needs a representative metric gate, enough traffic, and capacity headroom; low traffic hides tail failures

modules.title: Mesh Access Logs
modules.purpose: Debug request failures at the proxy
modules.productionQuestion: The app has no log for a failed request. Does the mesh?
modules.learningDelta: Access logs record proxy-level status, upstream, timing, and flags; they explain failures before the app sees them

modules.title: Mesh Tracing
modules.purpose: Connect proxy and application spans
modules.productionQuestion: Traces stop at the sidecar and do not show the upstream call. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Mesh tracing requires context propagation and proxy span generation; sampling and header handling decide continuity

modules.title: Sidecar Overhead
modules.purpose: Measure the cost of the mesh
modules.productionQuestion: Latency rose after enabling the mesh. How much is the sidecar?
modules.learningDelta: Sidecars add hops, CPU, memory, and connection pools; the cost is visible in per-hop latency and resource usage

modules.title: Ingress Gateway
modules.purpose: Terminate external traffic at the mesh edge
modules.productionQuestion: External traffic bypasses mesh policy and reaches pods directly. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: An ingress gateway provides a controlled entry point with TLS, routing, and policy; bypass paths defeat mTLS and observability

modules.title: Cross-Cluster Mesh
modules.purpose: Route across clusters without losing locality
modules.productionQuestion: A failover sends all traffic to one cluster and latency rises. What does the mesh know?
modules.learningDelta: Cross-cluster mesh discovers remote services; locality and failover policy decide whether traffic stays local

modules.title: Locality-Aware Load Balancing
modules.purpose: Keep traffic in the zone when it is healthy
modules.productionQuestion: Cross-zone traffic costs rise after a mesh rollout. What policy changed?
modules.learningDelta: Locality-aware balancing prefers local endpoints but fails over when local capacity or health is insufficient

modules.title: Mesh Failover
modules.purpose: Move traffic when a zone or cluster fails
modules.productionQuestion: A zone fails and Envoy keeps sending traffic to ejected endpoints. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Failover policy, priority groups, and health checks determine whether traffic moves; stale endpoints cause errors

modules.title: Envoy Retry Storm
modules.purpose: Stop retries from amplifying a dependency failure
modules.productionQuestion: A dependency fails for 5 seconds and request volume triples for 5 minutes. What caused it?
modules.learningDelta: Coordinated proxy retries amplify failure; retry budgets, jitter, and circuit breaking bound the amplification

modules.title: Policy Conflicts
modules.purpose: Predict which mesh policy wins
modules.productionQuestion: Two policies set different timeouts for the same service. Which one applies?
modules.learningDelta: Mesh policy precedence depends on scope and specificity; conflicting policies are hard to debug without a clear ownership model

modules.title: Envoy Admin and Stats
modules.purpose: Inspect the proxy without guessing
modules.productionQuestion: A request fails and the app has no error. What does Envoy admin show?
modules.learningDelta: Envoy admin exposes config dump, clusters, stats, and readiness; it is the fastest way to see proxy-level state

modules.title: Certificate Rotation
modules.purpose: Rotate mTLS identities without an outage
modules.productionQuestion: Certificates expire at midnight and the mesh starts failing handshakes. What rotation plan?
modules.learningDelta: Certificate rotation needs overlapping validity, trust bundles, and automated reload; short-lived certs reduce risk but require reliable automation

modules.title: Rolling Deployments
modules.purpose: Replace capacity without dropping below the minimum
modules.productionQuestion: A rolling deploy causes a brief 503 spike. What is the capacity math?
modules.learningDelta: Rolling deploys trade capacity for speed; minimum healthy and maximum surge determine whether the fleet survives the transition

modules.title: Blue-Green Deployments
modules.purpose: Cut over with a fast rollback path
modules.productionQuestion: A blue-green deploy is ready but the database migration is not reversible. Do you cut over?
modules.learningDelta: Blue-green gives fast traffic cutover and rollback, but shared state and schema changes can make the old environment unusable

modules.title: Canary Deployments
modules.purpose: Limit the blast radius of a bad release
modules.productionQuestion: A release has a bug that affects 1% of requests. How does a canary help?
modules.learningDelta: A canary exposes a small traffic slice to the new version and gates promotion on observed signals

modules.title: Feature Flags
modules.purpose: Decouple deploy from release
modules.productionQuestion: The code is deployed but the feature must stay off for one tenant. What do you use?
modules.learningDelta: Flags separate deploy from release; flag scope, defaults, and cleanup determine safety and long-term risk

modules.title: Canary with a Metric Gate
modules.purpose: Promote only when the canary proves itself
modules.productionQuestion: The canary passes error rate but fails at full rollout because of capacity. What gate was missing?
modules.learningDelta: A canary gate must cover error rate, latency, saturation, and capacity at the target scale, with enough traffic for confidence

modules.title: Automated Rollback
modules.purpose: Roll back before a human wakes up
modules.productionQuestion: A release raises 5xx at 3 a.m. How fast can rollback happen without a human?
modules.learningDelta: Automated rollback uses health and metric gates plus a tested rollback path; the recovery time is bounded by detection and artifact availability

modules.title: Blue-Green Database Migrations
modules.purpose: Change schema without breaking either version
modules.productionQuestion: Both blue and green must run during cutover. How do you migrate the database?
modules.learningDelta: Blue-green schema changes require expand/contract compatibility so both versions can read and write during the transition

modules.title: Expand/Contract Migrations
modules.purpose: Ship schema changes in safe steps
modules.productionQuestion: A column rename breaks the previous release. How do you sequence it?
modules.learningDelta: Expand/contract adds the new shape, backfills, dual-writes, then removes the old shape; each step is independently deployable

modules.title: Deployment Verification
modules.purpose: Prove the release works before shifting traffic
modules.productionQuestion: The deploy is green but the checkout path is broken. What verification was missing?
modules.learningDelta: Verification must exercise critical user paths, dependencies, and data, not just process health

modules.title: Smoke Tests
modules.purpose: Catch the obvious before users do
modules.productionQuestion: A new task starts and serves 200 on `/health` but 500 on checkout. What smoke test?
modules.learningDelta: Smoke tests exercise real dependencies and critical writes; health checks alone prove only process liveness

modules.title: Rollback vs Roll-Forward
modules.purpose: Choose the faster safe path under pressure
modules.productionQuestion: A bad release is live and the database has new rows. Do you roll back or fix forward?
modules.learningDelta: Rollback restores known code but may be incompatible with new data; roll-forward is faster only when the fix is understood and tested

modules.title: Traffic Shifting
modules.purpose: Move traffic in controlled increments
modules.productionQuestion: You need 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% with a gate at each step. How do you sequence it?
modules.learningDelta: Traffic shifting is a sequence of exposure steps with gates; step size trades detection time for blast radius

modules.title: Change Freezes
modules.purpose: Use freezes without creating a bigger risk
modules.productionQuestion: A freeze is active and a critical fix is needed. What is the exception path?
modules.learningDelta: Freezes reduce change risk but concentrate it; exceptions need review, rollback plans, and a clear owner

modules.title: Change Management That Helps
modules.purpose: Make change review faster and safer
modules.productionQuestion: Every change needs five approvals and incidents still happen. What should change review focus on?
modules.learningDelta: Good change management reviews blast radius, reversibility, observability, and ownership; approval count is not risk control

modules.title: GitOps
modules.purpose: Keep desired state reviewable and reversible
modules.productionQuestion: A manual console change disappears on the next sync. Why?
modules.learningDelta: GitOps makes Git the desired state; drift reconciliation overwrites manual changes, which is safety and a trap

modules.title: CI/CD Pipeline Design
modules.purpose: Make the pipeline fast enough to be used
modules.productionQuestion: The pipeline takes 90 minutes and teams bypass it. What do you optimize?
modules.learningDelta: Pipeline speed and reliability determine adoption; parallelism, caching, and staged gates reduce lead time without skipping safety

modules.title: Immutable Artifacts
modules.purpose: Build once and promote the same bits
modules.productionQuestion: Staging passed but production runs a different build. What went wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Immutable artifacts are built once, identified by digest, and promoted; rebuilding per environment changes the software

modules.title: Build Once, Deploy Many
modules.purpose: Keep environments identical
modules.productionQuestion: A config change requires a rebuild and staging diverges. How do you deploy the same artifact with different config?
modules.learningDelta: Configuration belongs outside the artifact; environment-specific config is injected at deploy time, with validation

modules.title: Config Drift
modules.purpose: Detect the setting that only production has
modules.productionQuestion: Staging and production behave differently after months of manual changes. How do you find drift?
modules.learningDelta: Drift is inevitable without reconciliation and comparison; config as code plus periodic diff reduces surprise

modules.title: Shadow Traffic
modules.purpose: Test a new version without user impact
modules.productionQuestion: You need production traffic to validate a rewrite but cannot affect users. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Shadow traffic mirrors requests to the new version and discards responses; it validates behavior but doubles load and risks side effects

modules.title: Dark Launches
modules.purpose: Release code before exposing the feature
modules.productionQuestion: The feature must be deployed for weeks before launch. How do you keep it dark?
modules.learningDelta: Dark launches deploy inactive code paths behind flags and verify them with synthetic or internal traffic

modules.title: Deploying During an Incident
modules.purpose: Decide whether a change helps or hurts
modules.productionQuestion: An incident is active and a fix is ready. Do you deploy now?
modules.learningDelta: Deploys during incidents add variables; prefer reversible config or flags, and deploy only with a clear hypothesis and rollback

modules.title: Canary Capacity Fallacy
modules.purpose: Test at the scale that will break
modules.productionQuestion: A canary passes at 5% traffic and the service fails at 100%. Why?
modules.learningDelta: A canary at low traffic does not exercise capacity, caches, locks, or downstream limits at full scale

modules.title: Schema Compatibility
modules.purpose: Keep old and new code working together
modules.productionQuestion: Old and new versions run side by side for an hour. What schema rules apply?
modules.learningDelta: Rolling and canary releases require backward and forward compatible schemas; readers must tolerate missing and extra fields

modules.title: Artifact Promotion
modules.purpose: Move a tested artifact through gates
modules.productionQuestion: A release is approved in staging; what exactly moves to production?
modules.learningDelta: Promotion moves the same immutable artifact and provenance, with environment config applied separately

modules.title: Deployment Frequency
modules.purpose: Increase speed without increasing risk
modules.productionQuestion: The team deploys monthly and every deploy is an incident. What changes first?
modules.learningDelta: Frequent small deploys reduce change size and improve recovery; the constraint is often test and rollback capability, not deploy tooling

modules.title: Lead Time for Changes
modules.purpose: Find the queue, not the coding time
modules.productionQuestion: A one-line fix takes two weeks to reach production. Where is the time spent?
modules.learningDelta: Lead time is dominated by queues, approvals, and test duration; optimize the constraint, not the average

modules.title: Rollback Data Loss
modules.purpose: Know what rollback cannot undo
modules.productionQuestion: A rollback restores the old code but the new code sent emails. What is irreversible?
modules.learningDelta: Rollback restores software, not external side effects; migrations, messages, and third-party calls need compensating actions

modules.title: Incident Command
modules.purpose: Run an incident instead of debugging in parallel
modules.productionQuestion: Five engineers are debugging and no one is communicating. What role is missing?
modules.learningDelta: Incident command assigns one coordinator, one communications owner, and one operations owner so investigation and communication do not compete

modules.title: Incident Roles
modules.purpose: Make ownership explicit under pressure
modules.productionQuestion: The database expert is also writing customer updates and misses the fix. How do you staff the incident?
modules.learningDelta: Separate command, operations, communications, and subject-matter roles; one person may hold two only in small incidents

modules.title: Communication Cadence
modules.purpose: Keep stakeholders informed without slowing response
modules.productionQuestion: The incident channel is silent for 40 minutes and support invents updates. What cadence?
modules.learningDelta: Regular updates at a fixed cadence reduce uncertainty; internal and external audiences need different detail

modules.title: Severity Levels
modules.purpose: Classify impact consistently and quickly
modules.productionQuestion: One team calls an outage SEV1 and another calls the same thing SEV3. Why does it matter?
modules.learningDelta: Severity drives paging, communication, and authority; criteria must be based on user impact and scope, not on cause

modules.title: Escalation
modules.purpose: Bring the right help at the right time
modules.productionQuestion: The on-call engineer is stuck and 30 minutes pass before backup is called. How do you escalate sooner?
modules.learningDelta: Escalation paths and triggers remove the social cost of asking; time-based and impact-based triggers work together

modules.title: Runbooks
modules.purpose: Turn diagnosis into repeatable steps
modules.productionQuestion: The same alert is handled differently by each engineer. What do you standardize?
modules.learningDelta: A runbook gives ordered checks, expected signals, safe actions, and escalation points for one alert

modules.title: Playbooks vs Runbooks
modules.purpose: Use the right level of guidance
modules.productionQuestion: A novel incident has no runbook. What playbook applies?
modules.learningDelta: Runbooks handle known alerts; playbooks give decision frameworks for unknown failures

modules.title: Incident Checklists
modules.purpose: Prevent skipped steps under stress
modules.productionQuestion: During a failover the team forgets to disable the retry storm. What prevents that?
modules.learningDelta: Checklists reduce omission under stress; they must be short, ordered, and tied to verification

modules.title: Blameless Postmortems
modules.purpose: Learn from failure without hiding it
modules.productionQuestion: The postmortem names the engineer who ran the command and no one shares details. What is wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Blameless analysis focuses on conditions and system design; blame suppresses the information needed to prevent recurrence

modules.title: Action Items That Land
modules.purpose: Turn findings into completed prevention
modules.productionQuestion: The last postmortem had 20 action items and none shipped. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Action items need an owner, due date, verification, and prioritization; unowned items are wishes

modules.title: On-Call Handoff
modules.purpose: Transfer context without dropping signals
modules.productionQuestion: A new shift starts and immediately asks what changed. What belongs in the handoff?
modules.learningDelta: A handoff covers active incidents, recent changes, risky deploys, expiring certificates, and known gaps

modules.title: Paging Fatigue
modules.purpose: Reduce pages without reducing detection
modules.productionQuestion: On-call receives 80 pages a week and misses the real one. What do you measure?
modules.learningDelta: Page load must be actionable and bounded; measure pages per shift and the fraction that lead to action, not raw alert count

modules.title: Error Budget Policy
modules.purpose: Decide when to stop shipping
modules.productionQuestion: The error budget is exhausted but the roadmap says ship. Who decides?
modules.learningDelta: An error budget policy pre-agrees consequences and exceptions; without it, the budget is only a dashboard

modules.title: Chaos Engineering
modules.purpose: Test failure assumptions safely
modules.productionQuestion: A dependency failure takes down the service despite redundancy. How do you find the gap before production?
modules.learningDelta: Chaos experiments test specific hypotheses with a bounded blast radius, stop conditions, and observability

modules.title: Game Days
modules.purpose: Rehearse response, not just failure
modules.productionQuestion: The team knows the system but has never practiced an incident together. What does a game day test?
modules.learningDelta: Game days combine a realistic scenario, roles, communications, and a debrief; they test people and process as much as technology

modules.title: Load Shedding in an Incident
modules.purpose: Decide what to drop under real pressure
modules.productionQuestion: The service is overloaded and every request is timing out. What do you shed first?
modules.learningDelta: Incident load shedding is a product decision made in advance: protect the critical path, drop low-value work, and communicate

modules.title: Degrading in an Incident
modules.purpose: Keep the promises that matter
modules.productionQuestion: Recommendation latency is causing checkout failures. What do you disable now?
modules.learningDelta: Incident degradation follows a pre-ranked dependency list and feature fallbacks; disabling fast is better than tuning slow

modules.title: Dependency Failure
modules.purpose: Contain a third-party outage
modules.productionQuestion: A payment provider is failing and your service returns 500 for all requests. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Dependency failures need isolation, fallback, and clear failure semantics; retrying a third party is not a strategy

modules.title: Retry Storms in Production
modules.purpose: Stop amplification during an active incident
modules.productionQuestion: A dependency blips and the whole platform melts down for 20 minutes. What is the first move?
modules.learningDelta: In a retry storm, reduce retries and load before tuning the dependency; retry budgets and breakers stop the feedback loop

modules.title: Cache Failure
modules.purpose: Survive losing the cache
modules.productionQuestion: Redis is down and the database immediately saturates. What is the incident plan?
modules.learningDelta: Cache failure shifts load to the origin; load shedding, negative caching, and a staged recovery prevent a second outage

modules.title: Database Failover Incident
modules.purpose: Run a failover without a reconnect storm
modules.productionQuestion: The database fails over and the app takes 10 minutes to recover. What is the sequence?
modules.learningDelta: Failover recovery depends on connection handling, DNS, retries, and capacity; the database may be healthy before the app is

modules.title: Multi-Region Failover
modules.purpose: Decide when a regional failover is worth it
modules.productionQuestion: One region is degraded but not down. Do you fail over and risk data loss?
modules.learningDelta: Regional failover trades availability for data loss and capacity; the decision needs RPO, capacity, and a tested runbook

modules.title: DNS Failure
modules.purpose: Diagnose the outage above your service
modules.productionQuestion: Nothing resolves and every service looks healthy. How do you confirm DNS?
modules.learningDelta: DNS failures look like many unrelated service failures; resolver, zone, and record health must be checked first

modules.title: Status Pages
modules.purpose: Communicate impact without speculation
modules.productionQuestion: Users report failures before the status page updates. What should it say?
modules.learningDelta: Status pages communicate known impact and next update time; they must not speculate on cause or blame a provider prematurely

modules.title: Customer Communication
modules.purpose: Give customers useful information under pressure
modules.productionQuestion: Support is pasting raw incident channel messages to customers. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Customer comms need impact, workaround, and next update; internal details and speculation increase harm

modules.title: Legal and Compliance During Incidents
modules.purpose: Know when an incident becomes a notification obligation
modules.productionQuestion: A breach may have exposed customer data. Who decides notification?
modules.learningDelta: Incident response must include legal and privacy counsel when data, contracts, or regulated data may be affected; deadlines start early

modules.title: Decision Logs
modules.purpose: Preserve why the team chose a risky action
modules.productionQuestion: The postmortem cannot explain why the team disabled the breaker. What was missing?
modules.learningDelta: Decision logs record options, rationale, owner, and time; they make incident reconstruction and review possible

modules.title: Toil Reduction
modules.purpose: Remove the work that scales with incidents
modules.productionQuestion: The team spends 40% of on-call on the same manual cleanup. How do you reduce it?
modules.learningDelta: Toil is repetitive, manual, and scalable work; measure it, automate the top tasks, and protect the time

modules.title: Incident Timeline
modules.purpose: Build the chronology that explains the outage
modules.productionQuestion: Two teams disagree about when the rollback happened. How do you settle it?
modules.learningDelta: A timeline combines alerts, deploys, decisions, and communications with synchronized timestamps and sources

modules.title: Severity Matrix
modules.purpose: Make severity objective across teams
modules.productionQuestion: Two incidents with the same impact get different responses. What does the matrix need?
modules.learningDelta: A severity matrix maps user impact, scope, and duration to response levels; it must be simple enough to use under pressure

modules.title: Postmortem Action Quality
modules.purpose: Write actions that prevent recurrence
modules.productionQuestion: The action is “be more careful” and the incident recurs. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Good actions change systems, have verification, and address contributing factors; human vigilance is not a control

modules.title: Incident Review
modules.purpose: Close the loop without reopening blame
modules.productionQuestion: The review becomes a debate about who caused it. How do you run it?
modules.learningDelta: Incident reviews examine timeline, contributing factors, and actions; facilitation and blameless framing keep the focus on systems

modules.title: VPC Fundamentals
modules.purpose: Place resources in the right network boundary
modules.productionQuestion: Two services cannot reach each other and both have public IPs. What is the first network boundary?
modules.learningDelta: A VPC is an isolated network with its own address space, route tables, and gateways; public IPs do not imply reachability

modules.title: Subnets and Route Tables
modules.purpose: Route traffic by destination and prefix
modules.productionQuestion: A new subnet has instances but no internet access. Which route is missing?
modules.learningDelta: A subnet is associated with one route table; the longest prefix match and target determine where traffic goes

modules.title: Route Table Blackholes
modules.purpose: Find a route that silently drops traffic
modules.productionQuestion: The instance has a route to the destination but packets disappear. What does the route target do?
modules.learningDelta: A route can point to a blackhole or an attachment that is unavailable; route presence does not guarantee forwarding

modules.title: NAT Gateway
modules.purpose: Give private subnets egress without inbound
modules.productionQuestion: Private tasks can reach S3 but not the internet. What is missing?
modules.learningDelta: NAT gateways provide outbound translation for private subnets; they are zonal, bandwidth-bound, and charge per GB

modules.title: Internet Gateway
modules.purpose: Make a public subnet actually public
modules.productionQuestion: A public subnet has a 0.0.0.0/0 route but still no internet. What is missing?
modules.learningDelta: An internet gateway attaches to the VPC and requires public IPs, routes, and security groups to work together

modules.title: Security Groups
modules.purpose: Allow traffic without opening the world
modules.productionQuestion: A new service cannot be reached from the load balancer. Which security group rule?
modules.learningDelta: Security groups are stateful allow lists; references between groups are safer than CIDR ranges

modules.title: Network ACLs
modules.purpose: Explain stateless subnet filtering
modules.productionQuestion: Security groups allow the traffic but a subnet ACL blocks the response. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Network ACLs are stateless and evaluated per subnet; ephemeral ports must be allowed in both directions

modules.title: VPC Peering vs Transit Gateway
modules.purpose: Choose a topology that scales beyond a few VPCs
modules.productionQuestion: Ten VPCs need full connectivity. Do you mesh peering or use a transit gateway?
modules.learningDelta: Peering is pairwise and non-transitive; Transit Gateway is a hub with attachments, route tables, and centralized policy

modules.title: Route Propagation
modules.purpose: Predict which route wins in a hub
modules.productionQuestion: Two attachments advertise the same prefix. Which path does traffic take?
modules.learningDelta: Longest prefix wins; for equal prefixes, route origin and propagation rules decide, and asymmetric paths are common

modules.title: Cross-Account Networking
modules.purpose: Connect accounts without broad trust
modules.productionQuestion: A shared service must be reachable from five accounts. How do you connect them safely?
modules.learningDelta: Cross-account networking uses resource policies, RAM, and centralized route/security ownership; account boundaries are real trust boundaries

modules.title: Resource Access Manager
modules.purpose: Share network resources without sharing accounts
modules.productionQuestion: You need one Transit Gateway for four accounts. How do you share it?
modules.learningDelta: RAM shares supported resources; consumers attach but ownership, quotas, and route policy stay with the owner

modules.title: PrivateLink
modules.purpose: Expose a service without network peering
modules.productionQuestion: A SaaS provider needs to reach your VPC without overlapping CIDRs. What do you use?
modules.learningDelta: PrivateLink exposes a service through an endpoint in the consumer VPC, avoiding CIDR overlap and broad routing

modules.title: VPC Endpoints
modules.purpose: Reach AWS services without NAT
modules.productionQuestion: S3 traffic is expensive through NAT. How do you keep it private?
modules.learningDelta: Gateway endpoints keep S3/DynamoDB traffic on the AWS network; interface endpoints use ENIs and security groups

modules.title: S3 Gateway Endpoints
modules.purpose: Remove S3 egress cost and NAT dependency
modules.productionQuestion: A private subnet uploads to S3 and the NAT bill is large. What changes?
modules.learningDelta: A gateway endpoint adds a route to S3 in the route table, avoiding NAT data processing charges

modules.title: Route 53 Resolver
modules.purpose: Resolve names across VPCs and on-premises
modules.productionQuestion: An on-premises service cannot resolve a private hosted zone. What do you configure?
modules.learningDelta: Resolver endpoints forward DNS between VPCs and on-premises; inbound and outbound endpoints serve different directions

modules.title: Private Hosted Zones
modules.purpose: Resolve internal names without public exposure
modules.productionQuestion: An internal service name resolves publicly. What is wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Private hosted zones are associated with VPCs and only resolve there; public zones resolve globally

modules.title: Direct Connect
modules.purpose: Plan private connectivity with bounded failure
modules.productionQuestion: The office link is down and the VPN backup is not taking traffic. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Direct Connect provides private dedicated connectivity but is not inherently diverse; BGP and backup paths determine failover

modules.title: Site-to-Site VPN
modules.purpose: Build a working backup path
modules.productionQuestion: The VPN tunnel is up but traffic does not flow. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: VPN requires matching tunnels, BGP or static routes, and security policies; tunnel state alone is not connectivity

modules.title: BGP for Hybrid Networking
modules.purpose: Understand path selection and failover
modules.productionQuestion: Two paths advertise the same prefix and traffic takes the slower one. Why?
modules.learningDelta: BGP selects paths by attributes such as local preference, AS path, and MED; failover depends on what changes

modules.title: Cross-AZ and Cross-Region Latency
modules.purpose: Put chatty traffic in the right failure domain
modules.productionQuestion: A service is 30ms slower after moving a dependency to another AZ. Is that expected?
modules.learningDelta: Cross-AZ adds a small latency and transfer cost; cross-region adds much more, and chatty protocols multiply both

modules.title: IAM Roles and Trust
modules.purpose: Give a workload credentials without keys
modules.productionQuestion: A service uses an access key in an environment variable. What replaces it?
modules.learningDelta: IAM roles use trust policies and temporary credentials; the workload assumes a role instead of storing keys

modules.title: Least Privilege
modules.purpose: Reduce permissions without breaking the service
modules.productionQuestion: A task role has `*:*` and security wants it reduced. How do you find the real permissions?
modules.learningDelta: Least privilege starts from observed access, uses scoped resources and conditions, and is verified in a non-production environment

modules.title: Confused Deputy
modules.purpose: Stop a service from acting for the wrong tenant
modules.productionQuestion: A cross-account role can be assumed by any account that knows its ARN. What condition fixes it?
modules.learningDelta: Confused-deputy protection uses source account, source ARN, or external ID conditions to bind trust to the intended caller

modules.title: KMS and Envelope Encryption
modules.purpose: Encrypt data without calling KMS per object
modules.productionQuestion: Each S3 object is encrypted with a KMS key and latency rises. What is the better pattern?
modules.learningDelta: Envelope encryption uses a data key for bulk data and KMS to protect the data key; direct KMS calls are for small secrets

modules.title: Encryption at Rest and in Transit
modules.purpose: Find the gap in the encryption story
modules.productionQuestion: Data is encrypted at rest but crosses a VPC in plaintext. What layer is missing?
modules.learningDelta: Encryption at rest and in transit are separate controls; TLS, mTLS, and service policies cover different paths

modules.title: Secrets Management
modules.purpose: Rotate credentials without redeploying everything
modules.productionQuestion: A database password is rotated and 30 services fail. How do you rotate safely?
modules.learningDelta: Secrets Manager or SSM can store and rotate secrets, but consumers must refresh or restart; rotation is a distributed deploy

modules.title: WAF and Shield Together
modules.purpose: Layer application and volumetric protection
modules.productionQuestion: A Layer 7 attack passes the WAF and saturates the origin. What layer failed?
modules.learningDelta: Shield protects volumetric L3/L4; WAF inspects L7 requests; neither replaces origin capacity or rate limiting

modules.title: Zero Trust
modules.purpose: Remove implicit trust inside the network
modules.productionQuestion: A compromised internal host can reach every service. What changes?
modules.learningDelta: Zero trust authenticates and authorizes each service request; network location is not identity

modules.title: Reachability Analyzer
modules.purpose: Test a path before changing production
modules.productionQuestion: You need to know whether a new route will work. Can you test without sending traffic?
modules.learningDelta: Reachability Analyzer evaluates configuration paths and returns the blocking component; it does not prove live traffic behavior

modules.title: VPC Flow Logs
modules.purpose: Prove whether packets arrived
modules.productionQuestion: The app sees no request and the client sees a timeout. Did the packet reach the instance?
modules.learningDelta: Flow logs record accepted and rejected flows at the ENI; they show direction, action, and bytes, but not payload

modules.title: NAT Gateway Scaling
modules.purpose: Avoid a zonal bandwidth bottleneck
modules.productionQuestion: Egress latency rises across all private subnets and NAT is the common component. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: NAT gateways scale per AZ and have bandwidth and port limits; one NAT for many AZs concentrates traffic and failure

modules.title: Egress Cost
modules.purpose: Find the traffic that leaves the cheapest boundary
modules.productionQuestion: The network bill is dominated by data transfer and no one knows which path. How do you attribute it?
modules.learningDelta: Egress costs differ by boundary: AZ, region, internet, and NAT processing; attribution needs flow data and tags

modules.title: HIPAA for Engineers
modules.purpose: Map technical controls to HIPAA obligations
modules.productionQuestion: A health-data workload needs HIPAA readiness. Which controls are actually required?
modules.learningDelta: HIPAA requires administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for protected health information; engineering owns access, audit, integrity, and transmission controls

modules.title: PHI Handling
modules.purpose: Keep protected health information out of the wrong systems
modules.productionQuestion: A log contains a diagnosis code and a patient identifier. Is that PHI?
modules.learningDelta: PHI is health information tied to an individual; identifiers plus health data create obligations across logs, backups, and vendors

modules.title: Business Associate Agreements
modules.purpose: Know when a vendor needs a BAA
modules.productionQuestion: You want to use a new observability vendor for a HIPAA workload. What must exist first?
modules.learningDelta: A BAA binds a vendor that handles PHI; without it, the vendor relationship is not compliant regardless of encryption

modules.title: Access Controls
modules.purpose: Prove least privilege and separation of duties
modules.productionQuestion: An auditor asks who can read production data. Can you answer in minutes?
modules.learningDelta: Access control evidence requires identity, role, approval, and review; shared accounts and standing admin rights break the story

modules.title: Audit Logs
modules.purpose: Capture who did what without capturing secrets
modules.productionQuestion: An audit trail is missing the actor for a privileged change. What fields are required?
modules.learningDelta: Audit logs need actor, action, target, time, outcome, and source, with integrity and retention; they must exclude secrets

modules.title: GDPR for Engineers
modules.purpose: Translate data-subject rights into system behavior
modules.productionQuestion: A user asks for their data. Which systems must answer?
modules.learningDelta: GDPR rights require data discovery, deletion, export, and lawful basis across primary stores, caches, logs, and backups

modules.title: Data Residency
modules.purpose: Keep data in the required jurisdiction
modules.productionQuestion: A customer contract requires EU-only storage. Which services and logs cross the boundary?
modules.learningDelta: Residency covers storage, processing, support access, backups, and telemetry; a regional bucket does not make the whole path local

modules.title: Right to Erasure
modules.purpose: Delete a person's data everywhere
modules.productionQuestion: A deletion request completes in the database but the data remains in logs and backups. What now?
modules.learningDelta: Erasure requires discovery and deletion or irreversible anonymization across primary data, derived data, logs, and backup policy

modules.title: Data Processing Agreements
modules.purpose: Define processor obligations before data flows
modules.productionQuestion: A new SaaS tool will process customer data. What must be agreed before rollout?
modules.learningDelta: A DPA defines processor scope, security, subprocessors, breach notice, and deletion; it is a prerequisite, not paperwork after launch

modules.title: SOC 2 for Engineers
modules.purpose: Produce evidence from real controls
modules.productionQuestion: An enterprise customer asks for SOC 2. Which controls need evidence?
modules.learningDelta: SOC 2 reports on security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy; evidence must come from operating controls

modules.title: ISO 27001
modules.purpose: Build a management system, not a document pile
modules.productionQuestion: The ISO audit finds policies but no risk treatment. What is missing?
modules.learningDelta: ISO 27001 requires a risk-based management system with ownership, treatment plans, and continual improvement

modules.title: PCI DSS Scope Reduction
modules.purpose: Keep card data out of most systems
modules.productionQuestion: The card-data environment includes the whole platform. How do you reduce scope?
modules.learningDelta: PCI scope follows cardholder data and connected systems; tokenization and segmentation shrink the audit boundary

modules.title: Data Classification
modules.purpose: Label data so controls can follow it
modules.productionQuestion: One bucket holds public, internal, and customer data. What is the classification?
modules.learningDelta: Classification drives access, encryption, retention, and incident handling; mixed datasets inherit the highest sensitivity

modules.title: Retention and Legal Hold
modules.purpose: Delete on schedule without destroying evidence
modules.productionQuestion: A legal hold arrives while the retention job is deleting records. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Retention schedules must be enforceable and suspendable; legal hold overrides deletion and requires evidence of preservation

modules.title: Audit Trails
modules.purpose: Make a sequence of events defensible
modules.productionQuestion: An auditor asks for the change history of a production role. Can you reconstruct it?
modules.learningDelta: Audit trails combine control-plane logs, approvals, and change records with synchronized time and integrity

modules.title: Evidence Collection
modules.purpose: Automate proof instead of screenshot hunting
modules.productionQuestion: The audit starts tomorrow and evidence lives in screenshots. How do you prepare?
modules.learningDelta: Evidence should be generated continuously from systems of record with timestamps, ownership, and retention

modules.title: Vendor Risk
modules.purpose: Assess a vendor before it becomes an incident
modules.productionQuestion: A critical vendor has no security review and an outage exposes customer data. What did you miss?
modules.learningDelta: Vendor risk covers security, availability, data handling, subcontractors, and exit; criticality determines depth

modules.title: Subprocessor Management
modules.purpose: Track the fourth parties in your data path
modules.productionQuestion: A vendor adds a subprocessor in another region and your residency promise breaks. How do you prevent it?
modules.learningDelta: Subprocessor obligations require notice, approval, flow-down terms, and a maintained inventory

modules.title: Incident Notification Timelines
modules.purpose: Start the clock before you understand the incident
modules.productionQuestion: A breach is suspected at 02:00. When does the notification clock start?
modules.learningDelta: Notification deadlines vary by regulation and jurisdiction; legal must be engaged as soon as a reportable incident is suspected

modules.title: Policy as Code
modules.purpose: Enforce controls before deployment
modules.productionQuestion: A production bucket is public despite a policy saying it must not be. How do you prevent it?
modules.learningDelta: Policy as code evaluates infrastructure before deploy and continuously detects drift; prevention is cheaper than audit findings

modules.title: Cost per Request
modules.purpose: Turn infrastructure spend into a unit metric
modules.productionQuestion: The monthly bill doubled but traffic only grew 20%. What changed per request?
modules.learningDelta: Cost per request separates volume growth from efficiency changes and exposes the expensive path

modules.title: Unit Economics
modules.purpose: Decide whether a feature is affordable at scale
modules.productionQuestion: A feature is profitable at 1k users and loses money at 1M. Which cost dominates?
modules.learningDelta: Unit economics combine compute, storage, network, and observability per unit of value; fixed costs hide until scale

modules.title: Autoscaling Policy Design
modules.purpose: Choose a policy that matches the workload
modules.productionQuestion: A service scales on CPU but the bottleneck is queue depth. What policy do you use?
modules.learningDelta: Scaling policies must follow the actual bottleneck metric and account for startup, cooldowns, and capacity limits

modules.title: The Cost of Headroom
modules.purpose: Price N+1 without pretending it is free
modules.productionQuestion: Finance asks why 40% of capacity is idle. How do you justify it?
modules.learningDelta: Headroom is insurance against failure and peaks; the right level depends on SLO, failure domain size, and traffic variability

modules.title: Warm Pools
modules.purpose: Reduce cold-start cost without paying for idle
modules.productionQuestion: Autoscaling takes 3 minutes to add capacity. Do you keep warm instances?
modules.learningDelta: Warm pools trade idle cost for faster scale-out; pool size must match the ramp rate, not the peak

modules.title: Scheduled Scaling
modules.purpose: Match known demand patterns
modules.productionQuestion: Traffic doubles every weekday at 9 a.m. Why wait for reactive scaling?
modules.learningDelta: Scheduled scaling handles predictable demand; it must be combined with reactive policies for surprises

modules.title: Scheduled Scaling Race Condition
modules.purpose: Stop a scheduled scale-down from fighting a spike
modules.productionQuestion: A scheduled scale-down at 18:00 collides with an organic surge and capacity collapses. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Scheduled and dynamic scaling can race; minimum capacity, cooldowns, and change freezes prevent the overlap

modules.title: Reserved Instances
modules.purpose: Buy commitment without locking in the wrong shape
modules.productionQuestion: RI coverage is 80% but the bill still rises. What changed?
modules.learningDelta: RIs discount steady-state usage but are tied to instance family, region, and term; workload drift wastes coverage

modules.title: Savings Plans
modules.purpose: Commit to spend without committing to instances
modules.productionQuestion: You need flexibility across instance families. Do RIs or Savings Plans fit?
modules.learningDelta: Savings Plans commit to usage for a discount and are more flexible than RIs, but still require accurate forecasting

modules.title: Spot Interruptions
modules.purpose: Use cheap capacity without losing the workload
modules.productionQuestion: Spot instances are 70% cheaper but tasks disappear. Which workloads fit?
modules.learningDelta: Spot capacity is interruptible with notice; stateless, checkpointed, and drainable workloads tolerate it

modules.title: Storage Lifecycle
modules.purpose: Move data to cheaper tiers before it grows
modules.productionQuestion: Storage cost grows every month and most objects are never read. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Lifecycle policies transition and expire data; retrieval cost and latency must match access patterns

modules.title: Observability Cost per Request
modules.purpose: Keep telemetry cost proportional to value
modules.productionQuestion: Observability is 25% of infrastructure cost and growing faster than traffic. Where do you cut?
modules.learningDelta: Telemetry has volume, cardinality, and retention costs; sampling and tiering should follow incident value, not default retention

modules.title: Rightsizing
modules.purpose: Match instance size to real usage
modules.productionQuestion: Half the fleet runs at 15% CPU and the bill is high. Why not downsize everything?
modules.learningDelta: Rightsizing uses utilization, memory, and burst behavior; averages hide peaks, and downsizing can break latency SLOs

modules.title: Load Testing
modules.purpose: Find the knee before production does
modules.productionQuestion: A load test passes at 10k RPS and production fails at 6k. What was unrealistic?
modules.learningDelta: Load tests must model traffic mix, data, dependencies, and open-loop arrival; a closed-loop test hides queueing and coordinated omission

modules.title: Capacity Models
modules.purpose: Forecast capacity from demand and service time
modules.productionQuestion: The quarterly forecast is a spreadsheet with no queueing. What is missing?
modules.learningDelta: Capacity models combine arrival rate, service time, concurrency, headroom, and failure domains; averages alone mislead

modules.title: Peak Event Planning
modules.purpose: Prepare for a known traffic spike
modules.productionQuestion: A marketing event will send 10× traffic in two weeks. What do you do now?
modules.learningDelta: Peak planning works backward from the event: forecast, load test, pre-scale, freeze changes, and staff the response

modules.title: Noisy Neighbor
modules.purpose: Isolate tenants without overprovisioning
modules.productionQuestion: One tenant's batch workload doubles the latency of everyone else. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Noisy neighbors need per-tenant quotas, isolation, or scheduling; shared pools maximize utilization and risk

modules.title: Queueing Headroom
modules.purpose: Convert utilization targets into latency budgets
modules.productionQuestion: The fleet runs at 85% CPU and p99 is unstable. What utilization target should you set?
modules.learningDelta: Latency rises nonlinearly near saturation; the safe target depends on variability and failure headroom, not a universal percentage

modules.title: Cost Allocation
modules.purpose: Attribute spend to the team that controls it
modules.productionQuestion: The bill is one number and no team owns it. How do you allocate cost?
modules.learningDelta: Cost allocation uses tags, accounts, and shared-cost splits; untagged resources and shared platforms need explicit rules

modules.title: Committed Use
modules.purpose: Balance discount and flexibility
modules.productionQuestion: A three-year commitment saves 40% but the workload may change. How do you decide?
modules.learningDelta: Commitments trade flexibility for discount; forecast confidence, term, and coverage determine the break-even

modules.title: Scale to Zero
modules.purpose: Save idle cost without breaking wake-up
modules.productionQuestion: A dev environment is idle 80% of the time. Can it scale to zero?
modules.learningDelta: Scale-to-zero saves idle cost but adds cold-start latency and state loss; production-critical paths usually need a floor

modules.title: Seasonal Forecasting
modules.purpose: Plan capacity across recurring peaks
modules.productionQuestion: Traffic grows 40% every December and the forecast is linear. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Forecasts need seasonality, growth, and uncertainty bands; capacity should be planned against a percentile, not a point estimate

modules.title: S3 us-east-1: The Control Plane That Took Down the Internet
modules.purpose: Replay a control-plane dependency failure and a restart storm
modules.productionQuestion: A storage service is down and the status page itself depends on it. What do you restore first?
modules.learningDelta: Control-plane dependencies and synchronized recovery can turn one service failure into a regional outage

modules.title: Kinesis us-east-1: Capacity Under a Regional Surge
modules.purpose: Analyze a managed-service capacity incident and its blast radius
modules.productionQuestion: A managed stream is throttling and every dependent service is failing. What is your first move?
modules.learningDelta: Managed-service limits are still capacity limits; dependent teams need isolation and backpressure before the service recovers

modules.title: AWS us-east-1: Network Congestion and the Retry Tax
modules.purpose: Reconstruct a regional network incident from customer signals
modules.productionQuestion: Your service is healthy but cross-AZ calls time out. How do you prove the network is the cause?
modules.learningDelta: Network congestion looks like application failure; retries and cross-AZ dependencies amplify the blast radius

modules.title: Lambda us-east-1: When the Control Plane Is the Product
modules.purpose: Separate data-plane health from control-plane failure
modules.productionQuestion: Existing functions serve traffic but new invocations cannot be created. Is the service up?
modules.learningDelta: Control-plane and data-plane health are different; recovery and scaling depend on the control plane even when the data path works

modules.title: Cloudflare 2019: One Regex, Global CPU Exhaustion
modules.purpose: Analyze a configuration change that exhausted edge CPU worldwide
modules.productionQuestion: A WAF rule passes review and then takes down every edge. How do you bound a global config change?
modules.learningDelta: Configuration is code with global blast radius; staged rollout, resource limits, and fast rollback are the controls

modules.title: Cloudflare 2020: A Backbone Change With Global Reach
modules.purpose: Trace a routing change through a global anycast network
modules.productionQuestion: A network change is supposed to affect one path and slows traffic everywhere. How do you verify before commit?
modules.learningDelta: Anycast and backbone changes have nonlocal effects; capacity and path validation must happen before global rollout

modules.title: Cloudflare 2022: Network Configuration and the Long Tail
modules.purpose: Diagnose a policy change that breaks a subset of routes
modules.productionQuestion: Most users are fine and one region is failing after a network policy change. How do you find the subset?
modules.learningDelta: Global configuration changes fail unevenly; per-region and per-route signals expose the subset that the aggregate hides

modules.title: Fastly 2021: A Config Push That Returned 503 Everywhere
modules.purpose: Replay a global edge configuration failure and recovery
modules.productionQuestion: A valid config passes validation and breaks every PoP. What is the safe deployment unit?
modules.learningDelta: Edge config needs canaries, independent validation, and a rollback path that does not depend on the failing system

modules.title: Facebook 2021: BGP Withdrawal and the DNS Death Spiral
modules.purpose: Analyze a self-isolating network failure
modules.productionQuestion: The network withdraws its own routes and the recovery tools depend on the network. How do you recover?
modules.learningDelta: Out-of-band access and independent recovery paths are mandatory when the failure removes the management plane

modules.title: GitHub 2018: A Network Partition and the Database
modules.purpose: Replay a partition that split the primary and the app
modules.productionQuestion: A network partition leaves two halves of the system with different views. Which writes do you accept?
modules.learningDelta: Partitions create split-brain risk; quorum and fencing decide which side may write, and recovery requires reconciliation

modules.title: GitHub 2020: DNS, TTLs, and the Recovery Window
modules.purpose: Analyze a DNS change that outlived its rollback
modules.productionQuestion: The DNS record is restored but users still fail for an hour. What controls the recovery window?
modules.learningDelta: DNS recovery is bounded by TTL, resolver behavior, and client caches; rollback does not imply immediate recovery

modules.title: GitLab 2017: The Backup That Did Not Restore
modules.purpose: Test recovery assumptions before an incident
modules.productionQuestion: The primary database is deleted and the five backup mechanisms fail in sequence. What do you verify?
modules.learningDelta: Backups are unproven until restored; replication, snapshots, and object storage each need independent validation

modules.title: Slack 2021: A Traffic Surge and the Cache Path
modules.purpose: Replay a demand surge that exposed a shared dependency
modules.productionQuestion: Traffic doubles on the first workday of the year and the service degrades. What breaks first?
modules.learningDelta: Surge incidents find the least elastic shared dependency; cache, DNS, and connection pools fail before CPU averages move

modules.title: Atlassian 2022: Restoring a Deleted Site
modules.purpose: Recover from a destructive control-plane action
modules.productionQuestion: An operator action deletes a site and the restore takes days. What controls prevent this?
modules.learningDelta: Destructive actions need soft delete, scoped permissions, and tested restore; control-plane mistakes are data-loss incidents

modules.title: Roblox 2021: Control Plane Congestion
modules.purpose: Analyze a cascading control-plane failure
modules.productionQuestion: The application is healthy but service discovery and configuration are failing. What do you stabilize first?
modules.learningDelta: Control-plane saturation can stop data-plane changes even when requests still succeed; recovery needs load reduction and sequencing

modules.title: Netflix 2012: The AZ Failure That Changed Architecture
modules.purpose: Learn how a real AZ failure drove isolation design
modules.productionQuestion: One AZ fails and the service degrades more than the capacity math predicts. Why?
modules.learningDelta: AZ isolation requires independent dependencies and capacity; a shared control plane or data store breaks the model

modules.title: Google Cloud 2019: A Network Policy Outage
modules.purpose: Reconstruct a cloud networking incident from customer impact
modules.productionQuestion: Regional traffic fails while compute instances are healthy. How do you localize a network control-plane fault?
modules.learningDelta: Cloud network control-plane faults can isolate healthy workloads; flow logs, route state, and provider status localize the failure

modules.title: Composite: The Region Failover That Ran Out of Capacity
modules.purpose: Test a failover plan against real capacity
modules.productionQuestion: The DR region is healthy but cannot absorb the primary's traffic. What did the plan miss?
modules.learningDelta: Regional failover must reserve capacity for the full active load, not just prove the standby exists

modules.title: Composite: DNS Failover Slower Than the RTO
modules.purpose: Reconcile DNS failover promises with client behavior
modules.productionQuestion: The record is updated in one minute but clients keep failing for 20. Why?
modules.learningDelta: DNS failover is bounded by the slowest resolver and client cache, not by the record's TTL alone

modules.title: Composite: The Canary That Passed at 5%
modules.purpose: Design a canary gate that tests full-scale behavior
modules.productionQuestion: The canary is clean at 5% and the full rollout fails at 100%. What was never tested?
modules.learningDelta: A canary must exercise capacity and shared-resource behavior at the target scale, not only error rate on a small slice

modules.title: Composite: The Retry Storm That Outlived the Failure
modules.purpose: Stop amplification after the dependency recovers
modules.productionQuestion: The dependency is healthy again but traffic keeps growing. What is still wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Retry amplification can persist after the trigger clears; retry budgets and breakers must be reduced before tuning the dependency

modules.title: Composite: The Hot Key at Peak
modules.purpose: Replay a partitioning failure with multiple valid fixes
modules.productionQuestion: One key is 50% of reads and the shard is at 95% CPU. Which fix do you choose under time pressure?
modules.learningDelta: Hot-key fixes differ in time-to-mitigate and staleness; local cache is fastest but changes consistency, salting needs a migration

modules.title: Composite: The TTL That Expired for Everyone
modules.purpose: Stop a synchronized cache expiry from taking down the database
modules.productionQuestion: A popular key expires and the database CPU goes to 100%. What do you do first?
modules.learningDelta: Stampede mitigation is layered: request coalescing protects immediately, jitter prevents recurrence, early refresh smooths the next expiry

modules.title: Composite: Consumer Lag After a Deploy
modules.purpose: Decide whether to scale, roll back, or shed
modules.productionQuestion: A deploy doubles processing time and lag grows by 10 minutes per hour. What is the first move?
modules.learningDelta: Consumer lag recovery depends on processing rate versus production rate; scaling cannot fix a slow single partition

modules.title: Composite: The Reconnect Storm After Failover
modules.purpose: Recover the application after the database is healthy
modules.productionQuestion: The database failed over successfully and the app is still down. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Database recovery is not application recovery; DNS, pools, and reconnect storms determine when traffic actually returns

modules.title: Composite: The IAM Change That Broke Production
modules.purpose: Find an authorization change during a broad outage
modules.productionQuestion: Half the services fail with access denied after a policy update. What do you roll back first?
modules.learningDelta: IAM changes are global configuration with delayed effects; audit logs and policy diffs localize the blast radius faster than service debugging

modules.title: Composite: The Monitoring Outage During an Incident
modules.purpose: Keep observability working when the platform is degraded
modules.productionQuestion: Dashboards are green and empty while users report failures. What is the first check?
modules.learningDelta: Monitoring the monitor is part of incident response; no-data and stale-data states must be explicit and alarmed

modules.title: Composite: The Certificate That Expired at Midnight
modules.purpose: Prevent a predictable outage from certificate expiry
modules.productionQuestion: TLS handshakes fail at 00:00 and no one is paged. What controls were missing?
modules.learningDelta: Certificate expiry is a scheduled outage; inventory, automated renewal, and expiry alerts are required controls

modules.title: Composite: NAT Port Exhaustion at Peak
modules.purpose: Diagnose connection failures with idle bandwidth
modules.productionQuestion: New outbound connections fail while throughput is low. What resource is exhausted?
modules.learningDelta: NAT port allocation and conntrack state can fail before bandwidth; connection churn is the driver

modules.title: Composite: The AZ Loss With N+0 Headroom
modules.purpose: Test whether N+1 is real in an emergency
modules.productionQuestion: One AZ fails and the remaining zones cannot carry peak. What was the actual headroom?
modules.learningDelta: Headroom must be measured after the largest failure, not on the pre-failure fleet

modules.title: Composite: The Message That Processed Twice
modules.purpose: Fix duplicate work without breaking throughput
modules.productionQuestion: A slow consumer exceeds visibility timeout and the same message is processed twice. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Visibility timeout must exceed processing time or be extended; idempotency is the backstop when duplicates happen

modules.title: Composite: The Mesh Retry Policy Nobody Owned
modules.purpose: Stop proxy retries from amplifying an outage
modules.productionQuestion: Every service retries three times and one dependency failure triples platform traffic. Where do you fix it?
modules.learningDelta: Retry policy is a shared dependency contract; mesh defaults and per-service overrides need ownership and budgets

modules.title: Composite: The Migration That Broke Rollback
modules.purpose: Plan a schema change that survives both versions
modules.productionQuestion: A release adds a required column and rollback fails because the old code cannot read it. What was missing?
modules.learningDelta: Schema changes must be backward and forward compatible during the rollout window; expand/contract sequences the risk

modules.title: Composite: The Feature Flag Default
modules.purpose: Contain a flag misconfiguration
modules.productionQuestion: A flag is created with the default on and the feature reaches all users. What controls prevent it?
modules.learningDelta: Flag defaults and targeting are production configuration; review, staged rollout, and a kill switch are required

modules.title: Composite: The Tag That Tripled the Bill
modules.purpose: Find a metric cardinality explosion
modules.productionQuestion: The observability bill triples after a release and dashboards slow down. What changed?
modules.learningDelta: A high-cardinality tag multiplies series and cost; cost anomalies should page the owning team, not just finance

modules.title: Composite: The Disk That Filled at 03:00
modules.purpose: Prevent a full disk from becoming a write outage
modules.productionQuestion: Logs fill the volume and the database stops accepting writes. What should have alerted first?
modules.learningDelta: Disk exhaustion is predictable with growth rate and retention; alerts must fire before the filesystem is full

modules.title: Composite: The Timeline That Blamed the Wrong Deploy
modules.purpose: Build a timeline with unreliable clocks
modules.productionQuestion: Logs, metrics, and deploy events disagree by minutes. How do you reconstruct causality?
modules.learningDelta: Clock skew and source ordering can invert cause and effect; timelines need source trust and time synchronization

modules.title: Composite: The Status Page That Lagged the Incident
modules.purpose: Communicate impact before certainty
modules.productionQuestion: Customers know about the outage before the status page updates. What is the right communication?
modules.learningDelta: Status communication can start with known impact and next update time before root cause is known

modules.title: Composite: The Payment Provider Outage
modules.purpose: Contain a critical third-party failure
modules.productionQuestion: A payment provider is down and checkout returns 500 for every cart. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Third-party failure needs isolation, fallback, and explicit failure semantics; not every flow should fail with the provider

modules.title: Composite: The Load Test That Lied
modules.purpose: Find measurement bias before trusting a capacity result
modules.productionQuestion: A load test passes at 20k RPS but production fails at 12k. What was measured wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Closed-loop load generators omit stalls and underreport tail latency; open-loop arrival and coordinated-omission correction are required

modules.title: Composite: The Autoscaler That Arrived Late
modules.purpose: Account for startup time in scaling
modules.productionQuestion: A traffic spike is over before new tasks become healthy. What should the policy have done?
modules.learningDelta: Autoscaling must account for startup latency and predict the ramp; reactive scaling on a short spike is too late

modules.title: Composite: The Cross-Region Bill
modules.purpose: Attribute a data-transfer cost spike
modules.productionQuestion: The network bill doubles after a service move and no one can name the path. How do you find it?
modules.learningDelta: Egress cost follows topology and chatter; flow data plus tags attribute cost to the service that creates it

modules.title: Composite: The Static Key in the Build
modules.purpose: Remove long-lived credentials from a pipeline
modules.productionQuestion: A build log contains an access key and the key has broad permissions. What is the response?
modules.learningDelta: Static keys in build systems require revocation, scoping, rotation, and workload identity; logs are a distribution channel

modules.title: Composite: The Audit Log That Expired
modules.purpose: Fix an evidence retention gap
modules.productionQuestion: An auditor asks for six months of admin activity and logs were kept for 30 days. What now?
modules.learningDelta: Audit retention must match regulatory and contractual windows; deletion policy is a compliance control

modules.title: Composite: The Erasure Request and the Backup
modules.purpose: Design deletion across derived and retained data
modules.productionQuestion: A user is erased from the primary database but remains in backups and logs. Is the request complete?
modules.learningDelta: Erasure requires a documented policy for backups and derived data, with anonymization or expiry rather than impossible immediate deletion

modules.title: Composite: The SOC 2 Evidence Scramble
modules.purpose: Turn controls into continuous evidence
modules.productionQuestion: The audit starts and half the evidence is screenshots from last quarter. What should have existed?
modules.learningDelta: Evidence must be generated from operating systems continuously, with timestamps and ownership

modules.title: Composite: The Scheduled Scale-Down During a Surge
modules.purpose: Prevent scheduled and dynamic scaling from fighting
modules.productionQuestion: A scheduled scale-down runs at 18:00 while a viral surge is starting. What guardrail was missing?
modules.learningDelta: Scheduled scaling must respect minimum capacity, cooldowns, and change freezes; dynamic demand can invalidate a schedule

modules.title: Composite: The Dead Letter Queue Nobody Read
modules.purpose: Operate a DLQ instead of hiding failures
modules.productionQuestion: A DLQ has 2 million messages and no one noticed. What is missing?
modules.learningDelta: A DLQ needs alerting, ownership, replay tooling, and retention; otherwise it converts visible failures into silent data loss

modules.title: Composite: The Pool Wait That Looked Like Slow Queries
modules.purpose: Separate queueing from execution time
modules.productionQuestion: Query latency is 2 seconds in the app but 20ms in the database. Where is the time?
modules.learningDelta: Client-side pool wait can dominate latency while the database is healthy; measure acquisition time separately

modules.title: Composite: The Slow Memory Leak
modules.purpose: Find a leak before OOM kills
modules.productionQuestion: Memory grows for days and the task restarts every 48 hours. What do you measure?
modules.learningDelta: Leak diagnosis compares heap over time and request volume; restarts hide the trend unless memory is graphed across restarts

modules.title: Composite: The DNS Cache That Outlived the Fix
modules.purpose: Account for client-side DNS caching
modules.productionQuestion: The record is fixed but one language runtime keeps failing. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Runtime DNS caching and connection pools can outlive record changes; restarts or cache TTLs determine recovery

modules.title: Composite: The Reshard That Broke Clients
modules.purpose: Move cache slots safely
modules.productionQuestion: A reshard starts and clients that do not follow redirects fail. What do you verify first?
modules.learningDelta: Cluster resharding requires redirect-aware clients, connection handling, and a rollback plan

modules.title: Composite: The Stale Read After a Write
modules.purpose: Fix read-after-write without abandoning replicas
modules.productionQuestion: A user saves a change and sees the old value on refresh. What is the cheapest correct fix?
modules.learningDelta: Read-your-writes needs a consistency boundary; sticky reads, version tokens, or primary reads for a window solve it at different costs

modules.title: Composite: The GOAWAY Storm
modules.purpose: Handle connection lifecycle during deploys
modules.productionQuestion: A deploy causes clients to reconnect in waves and latency spikes. What protocol behavior is involved?
modules.learningDelta: HTTP/2 GOAWAY and connection reuse interact with deploys; draining and jittered reconnect prevent a thundering herd

modules.title: Composite: The Sidecar That Stole the CPU
modules.purpose: Diagnose proxy overhead in a shared task
modules.productionQuestion: Latency rises after enabling the mesh and the app container is throttled. What is the cause?
modules.learningDelta: Sidecars share task CPU; limits and requests must account for proxy overhead or the main container starves

modules.title: Composite: The Endpoint Policy That Blocked Backups
modules.purpose: Debug a private endpoint policy
modules.productionQuestion: A backup job fails only in the private subnet after an endpoint policy change. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: VPC endpoint policies and route tables both gate private AWS access; allowing the route does not allow the action

modules.title: Composite: The Transit Gateway Route Loop
modules.purpose: Find asymmetric routing in a hub
modules.productionQuestion: Traffic enters through one attachment and returns through another, then disappears. What is wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Asymmetric routing breaks stateful inspection and return paths; TGW route tables must be symmetric by design

modules.title: Composite: The Backup Path That Never Activated
modules.purpose: Test BGP failover before the primary fails
modules.productionQuestion: The primary link fails and the backup stays idle. What attribute kept it unused?
modules.learningDelta: BGP failover depends on path attributes and health signals; an advertised backup is not a selected backup

modules.title: Composite: The Bill That Arrived After the Launch
modules.purpose: Attribute a post-launch cost surprise
modules.productionQuestion: A launch succeeds and the next bill is 3× forecast. Which usage dimension was missed?
modules.learningDelta: Launch economics need per-request cost, data transfer, storage growth, and telemetry; forecasts miss the fastest-growing dimension

modules.title: Composite: The Eviction Policy That Dropped the Working Set
modules.purpose: Protect the hot working set when memory is full
modules.productionQuestion: Redis is at maxmemory and hit rate falls; the eviction policy is allkeys-lru. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Eviction policy must match data value; allkeys policies evict hot data while volatile policies can refuse writes when nothing is evictable
